```{r filter_raw_detections, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# 1. Discard sequential detections from the same transmission ####

# Because of the high density of receivers, we are likely to have several detections of the same transmission on multiple receivers
# This is the whole idea behind telemetry positioning systems like the VPS
# This could complicate zone assignment if we frequently have the same transmission recorded on receivers in different zones
# If we assume that transmissions will be recorded first on the receiver to which the smolt is closest, we can also assume the smolt was in the same zone as the receiver that recorded the transmission first
# For each smolt, remove sequential detections w/ intervals < 20 s, which is the minimum tag transmission rate
raw_dets_orig <- raw_dets

raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Fish_ID, DateTime) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Fish_ID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(transmission_interval = as.numeric(DateTime - lag(DateTime)),
                same_transmission = if_else(transmission_interval < 20, 1, 0))

# How many recorded detections were identified as being transmission duplicates?
raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::summarise(sum = sum(same_transmission, na.rm = TRUE))

# Remove duplicate transmissions
raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::filter(same_transmission == 0 | is.na(same_transmission))

# Repeat the process one more time (there's still 3 sequential detections that are < 20 s apart)
raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Fish_ID, DateTime) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Fish_ID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(transmission_interval = as.numeric(DateTime - lag(DateTime)),
                same_transmission = if_else(transmission_interval < 20, 1, 0))

# How many recorded detections were identified as being transmission duplicates?
raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::summarise(sum = sum(same_transmission, na.rm = TRUE))

# Remove duplicate transmissions
raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::filter(same_transmission == 0 | is.na(same_transmission)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(same_transmission,
                   transmission_interval))


# Add Date and Time of release to raw dets
foo <- VPS.smolts %>%
  dplyr::select(Fish_ID, Tag_ID, Release_DateTime, Release_DateTime_UTC) %>%
  dplyr::rename(DateTime = Release_DateTime,
                DateTime_UTC = Release_DateTime_UTC) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Zone = "2",
                Station = "Release",
                Receiver = "Release",
                Tag_ID = as.character(Tag_ID))

raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::relocate(Fish_ID, Tag_ID, DateTime, DateTime_UTC, Station, Receiver, Zone)

foo <- foo %>%
  dplyr::relocate(Fish_ID, Tag_ID, DateTime, DateTime_UTC, Station, Receiver, Zone)

raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(foo)

remove(foo)

raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Fish_ID, DateTime)

# 2. Identify potential mortality or tag shedding ####

# The high-density array of receivers allows us to identify periods where smolts did not move, suggesting possible mortality or tag shedding
# These occurrences could have an effect on estimating passage rates
# For instance, if a smolt has died or a tag shed in the "attempt zone", it will be included as part of the risk set for passage rates
# Thus, these detections should be discarded

# Start by examining detection histories for each smolt
# For the purpose of plotting detection histories, arrange station levels from south to north
raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Stations_Ordered = factor(Station, levels = c("R25", "R26", "R24", "Release", "R22", "R21", "R20", "R19", "R18", "R17", "R16", "R15",
                                                              "R14", "R13", "R12", "R11", "R10", "R09", "R27", "R28", "R29", "R30", "R39", "R38",
                                                              "R31", "R32", "R33", "R08", "R00", "R07", "R06", "R05", "R04", "R03", "R02", "R01",
                                                              "R34", "R37", "R35", "R36")),
                Areas_Ordered = case_when(Stations_Ordered == "R25" | Stations_Ordered == "R26" | Stations_Ordered == "R24" ~ "Lake",
                                           Stations_Ordered == "Release" | Stations_Ordered == "R22" | Stations_Ordered == "R21" |
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R20" | Stations_Ordered == "R19" | Stations_Ordered == "R18" | 
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R17" | Stations_Ordered == "R16" | Stations_Ordered == "R15" |
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R14" | Stations_Ordered == "R13" | Stations_Ordered == "R12" |
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R11" | Stations_Ordered == "R10" | Stations_Ordered == "R09" ~ "Outlet_West",
                                           Stations_Ordered == "R27" | Stations_Ordered == "R28" | Stations_Ordered == "R29" |
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R30" | Stations_Ordered == "R39" | Stations_Ordered == "R38" |
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R31" | Stations_Ordered == "R32" | Stations_Ordered == "R33" ~ "Outlet_East",
                                          Stations_Ordered == "R08" | Stations_Ordered == "R00" | Stations_Ordered == "R07" |
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R06" | Stations_Ordered == "R05" | Stations_Ordered == "R04" |
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R03" | Stations_Ordered == "R02" | Stations_Ordered == "R01" ~ "Attempt",
                                           Stations_Ordered == "R34" | Stations_Ordered == "R37" | Stations_Ordered == "R35" |
                                             Stations_Ordered == "R36" ~ "Passed")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Areas_Ordered = factor(Areas_Ordered, levels = c("Passed", "Attempt", "Outlet_North", "Outlet_East", "Outlet_West", "Lake")))


# Write a function that plots detection history for each smolt w/ time on X and receiver station on Y
# Packages
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(rlang)

save_individual_plots <- function(data,
                                  id_col,
                                  x_col,
                                  y_col,
                                  color_col = NULL,   # NEW: column to color points
                                  out_dir = "individual_plots",
                                  width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300,
                                  device = "png",
                                  plot_fun = NULL) {

  id_sym     <- rlang::ensym(id_col)
  x_sym      <- rlang::ensym(x_col)
  y_sym      <- rlang::ensym(y_col)
  color_sym  <- if (!is.null(color_col)) rlang::ensym(color_col) else NULL

  dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  gdf <- data %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::arrange(!!id_sym, !!x_sym) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(!!id_sym)

  chunks <- gdf %>% dplyr::group_split(.keep = TRUE)
  ids    <- gdf %>% dplyr::group_keys() %>% dplyr::pull(!!id_sym)

  make_safe <- function(x) gsub("[^[:alnum:]_.-]+", "_", as.character(x))

  purrr::walk2(chunks, ids, function(df_i, id_val) {
    safe_id <- make_safe(id_val)

    p <- if (is.null(plot_fun)) {
      if (is.null(color_sym)) {
        ggplot(df_i, aes(x = !!x_sym, y = !!y_sym)) +
          geom_point(size = 0.8, color = "black")
      } else {
        ggplot(df_i, aes(x = !!x_sym, y = !!y_sym, color = !!color_sym)) +
          geom_point(size = 0.8)
      } +
        labs(
          title = paste("ID:", id_val),
          x = rlang::as_name(x_sym),
          y = rlang::as_name(y_sym),
          color = if (!is.null(color_sym)) rlang::as_name(color_sym) else NULL
        ) +
        manuscript_theme +
        theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
              legend.position = "right")
    } else {
      plot_fun(df_i, id_val)
    }

    ggsave(
      filename = file.path(out_dir, paste0("ID-", safe_id, ".", device)),
      plot = p, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi, device = device
    )
  })

  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

```{r filter_problematic_detections, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# smolt 283 - censor on 2014-05-20 15:57:18 - no evidence of passage, no downstream detections
```

```{r identify_zone_transitions, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# Identify timing of zone transitions 

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(lubridate)
})

# build_zone_intervals_from_detections()

# Rules:

# - Maintain previous zone until a new zone has >= min_dwell_minutes of continuous detections.

# - First segment per individual (release), always Zone "2":
#     * Exempt from "one row"/short-run absorption.
#     * If the second segment is not Zone 2, time from first tstart to second's tstart is still credited to Zone 2.

# - Zone 4 terminal rule:
#     * Zone 4 can only occur as the final segment.
#     * Any Zone 4 segment followed by another segment is absorbed into an adjacent non-4 zone
#       (prefer previous; if none, absorb into next). Then adjacent equal zones are collapsed.

# - Transition time is the first detection in the confirmed new zone.

# Outputs:
#   $intervals: ID, Zone, tstart, tstop, n_positions, zone_interval_index, zone_interval_id
#   $rows     : original rows labeled with zone_interval_index, zone_interval_id

build_zone_intervals_from_detections <- function(
    df,
    id_col            = "ID",
    time_col          = "DateTime",
    zone_col          = "Zone",
    min_dwell_minutes = 5,
    tz                = "Canada/Pacific",
    # infer Zone 1 only from gaps > X minutes
    gap_to_zone1_minutes = 5
) {
  stopifnot(all(c(id_col, time_col, zone_col) %in% names(df)))
  
  library(dplyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(tidyr)
  
  # Minimal working copy (retain original row index for stable ordering)
  dat <- df %>%
    transmute(
      .id   = .data[[id_col]],
      .time = .data[[time_col]],
      .zone = .data[[zone_col]],
      .orig_row = row_number()
    )
  
  if (!inherits(dat$.time, "POSIXct")) {
    dat$.time <- as.POSIXct(dat$.time, tz = tz)
  }
  
  dat <- dat %>%
    arrange(.id, .time, .orig_row) %>%
    group_by(.id) %>%
    mutate(.row = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # For terminal inference, we need each ID's final detection time (from original data)
  id_last_time <- dat %>%
    group_by(.id) %>%
    summarise(final_time = max(.time), .groups = "drop")
  
  # Collapse consecutive equal zones into raw segments for a single ID
  collapse_segments_one <- function(df_id, id_val) {
    if (nrow(df_id) == 0L) {
      return(tibble(.id = id_val, zone = df_id$.zone[0], start_time = as.POSIXct(character()),
                    end_time = as.POSIXct(character()), n_positions = integer(),
                    .rows_idx = list()))
    }
    r <- rle(df_id$.zone)
    seg_id <- inverse.rle(list(values = seq_len(length(r$lengths)), lengths = r$lengths))
    df_id$._seg_tmp <- seg_id
    
    out <- df_id %>%
      group_by(._seg_tmp) %>%
      summarise(
        .id         = id_val,
        zone        = first(.zone),
        start_time  = first(.time),
        end_time    = last(.time),
        n_positions = n(),
        .rows_idx   = list(.row),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      arrange(start_time) %>%
      dplyr::select(-._seg_tmp)
    
    out$duration_min <- as.numeric(difftime(out$end_time, out$start_time, units = "mins"))
    out
  }
  
  # Hysteresis with release-row exemption:
  # Keep first segment even if short (as long as it's Zone "2").
  enforce_dwell_one <- function(seg_tbl, dwell_min) {
    n <- nrow(seg_tbl)
    if (n <= 1) return(seg_tbl)
    
    # FIRST: Do NOT absorb forward if it's Zone "2" (release).
    if (seg_tbl$duration_min[1] < dwell_min && n >= 2 && !(as.character(seg_tbl$zone[1]) %in% c("2", 2))) {
      seg_tbl$zone[1] <- seg_tbl$zone[2]
    }
    
    # LAST: absorb short last backward
    if (seg_tbl$duration_min[n] < dwell_min && n >= 2) {
      seg_tbl$zone[n] <- seg_tbl$zone[n-1]
    }
    
    # Forward pass with dwell confirmation
    res <- seg_tbl[0, ]
    current_zone <- seg_tbl$zone[1]
    cur <- seg_tbl[1, ]
    
    for (i in 2:n) {
      cand <- seg_tbl[i, ]
      if (identical(as.character(cand$zone), as.character(current_zone))) {
        # extend current
        cur$end_time    <- cand$end_time
        cur$n_positions <- cur$n_positions + cand$n_positions
        cur$.rows_idx[[1]] <- c(cur$.rows_idx[[1]], cand$.rows_idx[[1]])
        cur$duration_min <- as.numeric(difftime(cur$end_time, cur$start_time, units = "mins"))
      } else {
        # confirm only if dwell >= threshold
        if (cand$duration_min >= min_dwell_minutes) {
          res <- bind_rows(res, cur)
          cur <- cand
          current_zone <- cand$zone
        } else {
          # absorb candidate into current
          cur$end_time    <- cand$end_time
          cur$n_positions <- cur$n_positions + cand$n_positions
          cur$.rows_idx[[1]] <- c(cur$.rows_idx[[1]], cand$.rows_idx[[1]])
          cur$duration_min <- as.numeric(difftime(cur$end_time, cur$start_time, units = "mins"))
        }
      }
    }
    res <- bind_rows(res, cur)
    
    # Collapse any accidental adjacencies (same zone back-to-back)
    if (nrow(res) > 1) {
      out <- res[1, ]
      for (i in 2:nrow(res)) {
        if (identical(as.character(res$zone[i]), as.character(out$zone[nrow(out)]))) {
          out$end_time[nrow(out)]    <- res$end_time[i]
          out$n_positions[nrow(out)] <- out$n_positions[nrow(out)] + res$n_positions[i]
          out$.rows_idx[[nrow(out)]] <- c(out$.rows_idx[[nrow(out)]], res$.rows_idx[[i]])
          out$duration_min[nrow(out)] <- as.numeric(difftime(out$end_time[nrow(out)],
                                                             out$start_time[nrow(out)], units = "mins"))
        } else {
          out <- bind_rows(out, res[i, ])
        }
      }
      res <- out
    }
    res
  }
  
  # Zone 4 terminal enforcement: any zone 4 that is NOT last gets absorbed and collapsed
  terminalize_zone4_one <- function(seg_tbl) {
    n <- nrow(seg_tbl)
    if (n <= 1) return(seg_tbl)
    if (!any(as.character(seg_tbl$zone) %in% c("4", 4))) return(seg_tbl)
    
    # Work on a copy we can mutate
    res <- seg_tbl
    
    # Identify zone==4 that are not last; absorb them
    idx4 <- which(as.character(res$zone) %in% c("4", 4))
    idx4_not_last <- idx4[idx4 < nrow(res)]
    
    if (length(idx4_not_last)) {
      for (i in idx4_not_last) {
        if (i > 1) {
          # absorb into previous zone
          res$zone[i] <- res$zone[i - 1]
        } else {
          # if first is 4 and not last, absorb into next zone
          res$zone[i] <- res$zone[i + 1]
        }
      }
    }
    
    # Collapse adjacent equal zones and recompute summaries
    if (nrow(res) == 1) return(res)
    
    out <- res[1, ]
    for (i in 2:nrow(res)) {
      if (identical(as.character(res$zone[i]), as.character(out$zone[nrow(out)]))) {
        out$end_time[nrow(out)]    <- res$end_time[i]
        out$n_positions[nrow(out)] <- out$n_positions[nrow(out)] + res$n_positions[i]
        out$.rows_idx[[nrow(out)]] <- c(out$.rows_idx[[nrow(out)]], res$.rows_idx[[i]])
        out$duration_min[nrow(out)] <- as.numeric(difftime(out$end_time[nrow(out)],
                                                           out$start_time[nrow(out)], units = "mins"))
      } else {
        out <- bind_rows(out, res[i, ])
      }
    }
    out
  }
  
  # NEW: drop Zone-1 detections and infer Zone-1 from:
  #  (a) gaps between two Zone-2 segments, and
  #  (b) a terminal gap after the last Zone-2 if later detections exist (final_time > last Z2 end)
  insert_inferred_zone1 <- function(seg_tbl, gap_min, final_time) {
    if (nrow(seg_tbl) <= 1) {
      # If single segment and it's Z2, allow terminal Zone-1 only if final_time > end
      if (nrow(seg_tbl) == 1 &&
          as.character(seg_tbl$zone[1]) %in% c("2", 2) &&
          !is.na(final_time)) {
        gap_minutes <- as.numeric(difftime(final_time, seg_tbl$end_time[1], units = "mins"))
        if (!is.na(gap_minutes) && gap_minutes > gap_min) {
          z1 <- seg_tbl[1, ]
          z1$zone         <- "1"
          z1$start_time   <- seg_tbl$end_time[1]
          z1$end_time     <- final_time
          z1$n_positions  <- 0L
          z1$.rows_idx    <- list(integer(0))
          z1$duration_min <- as.numeric(difftime(z1$end_time, z1$start_time, units = "mins"))
          return(bind_rows(seg_tbl, z1))
        }
      }
      return(seg_tbl)
    }
    
    # Ignore any actual Zone-1 segments
    res <- seg_tbl %>% filter(!(as.character(zone) %in% c("1", 1)))
    if (nrow(res) == 0) return(seg_tbl[0,]) # shouldn't happen, but keep type
    
    out <- res[0, ]
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(res) - 1)) {
      cur <- res[i, ]
      nxt <- res[i + 1, ]
      out <- bind_rows(out, cur)
      
      # Case (a): Z2 ... gap ... Z2
      if (as.character(cur$zone) %in% c("2", 2) &&
          as.character(nxt$zone) %in% c("2", 2)) {
        gap_minutes <- as.numeric(difftime(nxt$start_time, cur$end_time, units = "mins"))
        if (!is.na(gap_minutes) && gap_minutes > gap_min) {
          z1 <- cur
          z1$zone         <- "1"
          z1$start_time   <- cur$end_time
          z1$end_time     <- nxt$start_time
          z1$n_positions  <- 0L
          z1$.rows_idx    <- list(integer(0))
          z1$duration_min <- as.numeric(difftime(z1$end_time, z1$start_time, units = "mins"))
          out <- bind_rows(out, z1)
        }
      }
    }
    # append last non-1 segment
    out <- bind_rows(out, res[nrow(res), , drop = FALSE])
    
    # Case (b): terminal Zone-1 after the last Z2, only if final_time > last Z2 end
    last_seg <- tail(out, 1)
    if (as.character(last_seg$zone) %in% c("2", 2) && !is.na(final_time)) {
      gap_minutes <- as.numeric(difftime(final_time, last_seg$end_time, units = "mins"))
      if (!is.na(gap_minutes) && gap_minutes > gap_min) {
        z1 <- last_seg
        z1$zone         <- "1"
        z1$start_time   <- last_seg$end_time
        z1$end_time     <- final_time
        z1$n_positions  <- 0L
        z1$.rows_idx    <- list(integer(0))
        z1$duration_min <- as.numeric(difftime(z1$end_time, z1$start_time, units = "mins"))
        out <- bind_rows(out, z1)
      }
    }
    out
  }
  
  # Split by ID
  splits <- dat %>% group_by(.id) %>% group_split()
  keys   <- dat %>% group_by(.id) %>% group_keys()
  
  # Raw segments
  raw_segments <- purrr::map2_dfr(splits, keys$.id, collapse_segments_one)
  
  # Apply hysteresis per ID (with release exemption)
  segments_hysteresis <- raw_segments %>%
    group_by(.id) %>%
    group_split() %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(~ enforce_dwell_one(.x, min_dwell_minutes))
  
  # Apply Zone 4 terminal rule per ID
  segments <- segments_hysteresis %>%
    group_by(.id) %>%
    group_split() %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(terminalize_zone4_one)
  
  # Infer Zone-1 from Z2-bounded gaps and terminal Z2→final_time gaps (ignore Z1 detections)
  segments <- segments %>%
    left_join(id_last_time, by = c(".id" = ".id")) %>%
    group_by(.id, final_time) %>%
    group_split() %>%
    purrr::map2_dfr(.x = ., .y = purrr::map(., ~ unique(.x$final_time)[1]),
                    .f = ~ insert_inferred_zone1(.x %>% dplyr::select(-final_time),
                                                 gap_min   = gap_to_zone1_minutes,
                                                 final_time = .y)) %>%
    arrange(.id, start_time)
  
  # Build intervals with tstart, tstop
  build_intervals_one <- function(seg_tbl) {
    seg_tbl %>%
      arrange(start_time) %>%
      mutate(
        tstart = start_time,
        next_start = dplyr::lead(start_time),
        last_end   = end_time,
        tstop  = coalesce(next_start, last_end)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(.id, zone, tstart, tstop, n_positions)
  }
  
  intervals <- segments %>%
    group_by(.id) %>%
    group_split() %>%
    purrr::map_dfr(build_intervals_one)
  
  # Per-ID, per-zone running index + label "Z{zone}_{index}"
  intervals <- intervals %>%
    mutate(zone_chr = as.character(zone)) %>%
    group_by(.id, zone_chr) %>%
    arrange(tstart, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      zone_interval_index = row_number(),
      zone_interval_id    = paste0("Z", zone_chr, "_", zone_interval_index)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(.id, zone, tstart, tstop, n_positions,
                  zone_interval_index, zone_interval_id)
  
  # Map interval labels back to rows
  segments_labeled <- segments %>%
    group_by(.id) %>%
    arrange(start_time, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(seg_id = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  intervals_lookup <- intervals %>%
    group_by(.id) %>%
    arrange(tstart, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(seg_id = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::select(.id, seg_id, zone_interval_id, zone_interval_index)
  
  rows_map <- segments_labeled %>%
    dplyr::select(.id, seg_id, .rows_idx) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(.rows_idx, names_repair = "minimal") %>%
    rename(.row = .rows_idx) %>%
    left_join(intervals_lookup, by = c(".id", "seg_id"))
  
  dat_out <- dat %>%
    left_join(rows_map %>% dplyr::select(.id, .row, zone_interval_id, zone_interval_index),
              by = c(".id", ".row"))
  
  # Prepare outputs
  intervals_out <- intervals %>%
    arrange(.id, tstart) %>%
    rename(!!id_col := .id,
           !!zone_col := zone)
  
  rows_out <- dat_out %>%
    arrange(.id, .time, .row) %>%
    dplyr::select(!!id_col := .id,
                  !!time_col := .time,
                  !!zone_col := .zone,
                  zone_interval_index,
                  zone_interval_id)
  
  list(intervals = intervals_out, rows = rows_out)
}


raw_dets <- raw_dets %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Fish_ID, DateTime)

zone_transitions_list <- build_zone_intervals_from_detections(
  df       = raw_dets,
  id_col   = "Fish_ID",
  time_col = "DateTime",
  zone_col = "Zone",
  min_dwell_minutes = 3,
  tz = "Canada/Pacific",
  gap_to_zone1_minutes = 10
)

# Zone transition intervals
zone_intervals <- zone_transitions_list$intervals

# Zone transition rows
zone_rows <- zone_transitions_list$rows

# We should be able to mainly work with the intervals data.
# Format intervals data for cox PH models
zone_intervals <- zone_intervals %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Fish_ID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tstart_timestamp = tstart,
                tstop_timestamp = tstop,
                tstart_release = as.numeric(difftime(tstart_timestamp, min(tstart_timestamp), units = "hours")),
                tstop_release = as.numeric(difftime(tstop_timestamp, min(tstart_timestamp), units = "hours")))

# Create a column that identifies the next zone of occupation
# Zone_next == NA indicates terminal zone
zone_intervals <- zone_intervals %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Fish_ID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Zone_next = lead(Zone))

# Create tstart and tstop columns for each zone interval
zone_intervals <- zone_intervals %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Fish_ID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tstart_interval = min(tstart_release),
                tstop_interval = tstop_release - tstart_release)

# Arrange columns
zone_intervals <- zone_intervals %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Fish_ID, tstart_timestamp) %>%
  dplyr::select(Fish_ID, tstart_interval, tstop_interval, Zone, Zone_next, zone_interval_index, zone_interval_id, tstart_timestamp, tstop_timestamp,
                tstart_release, tstop_release)
```

```{r add_covariates_to_zone_intervals, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# 3. Time-varying fence status ####

# The fence status (open vs. closed) needs to be incorporated before any other step so that we can identify risk states associated with periods that the fence was open "at risk" vs closed "not at risk" (for the multi-state model)

# First, create a new data set where each row is a new fence status
library(data.table)

# Convert to data.table for easier grouping by run-length encoding
dt <- as.data.table(fence.openings)

# Create a group identifier for runs of the same fence_status
dt[, group := rleid(fence_status)]

# Collapse intervals where fence_status is "open"
collapsed <- dt[, .(
  Start = min(Start),
  End = max(End),
  fence_status = first(fence_status)
), by = group][, .(Start, End, fence_status)]  # Drop the 'group' column

collapsed <- collapsed %>%
  dplyr::rename(DateTime_Start = Start,
                DateTime_End = End)

collapsed <- as_tibble(collapsed)

# Check that this worked as intended by referencing the fence.openings data set

for (i in 1:nrow(zone_intervals_coxPH)) {
  fish <- zone_intervals_coxPH[i, ]
  start <- fish$tstart_timestamp
  stop <- fish$tstop_timestamp
  
  fence_sub <- collapsed %>%
    dplyr::filter(DateTime_End > start, DateTime_Start < stop) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(interval_id = fish$interval_id,
                  tchange = as.numeric(difftime(DateTime_Start, start, units = "hours"))) %>%
    dplyr::select(interval_id, tchange, fence_status)
  
  fence_events_list[[i]] <- fence_sub
}

fence_events_all <- bind_rows(fence_events_list) %>%

# For some reason, tchange = 0 is negative for the first fence status in every interval,
# even though the fence status at the start of each interval was correctly assigned.

# For example, the first observation for smolt 100 (100_Z2_1, since release was in zone 2) has a tchange value of -0.41666667 and a fence status of 'closed'. 
# This smolt was release on Apr. 30 at 00:25:00, and the fence was closed 25 minutes (~0.417 hours) earlier at 00:00:00. 
# So, the fence_status is correct, but the value of -0.417 in tchange is indicating that the fence was closed 0.417 hours (25 minutes) before the smolt was released.
# Change all negative values for tchange to 0

fence_events_all <- fence_events_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tchange = if_else(tchange < 0, 0, tchange))

# Stack sunrise/sunset into long format
diel_changes <- solar.data %>%
  dplyr::select(sunrise, sunset) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "type", values_to = "change_time") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(change_time) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diel_period = ifelse(type == "sunrise", "day", "night"))

str(diel_changes)

# Assign each smolt an initial diel period at release
# Function to classify diel period at a given datetime
get_diel_period <- function(datetime, solar.data) {
  date <- as.Date(datetime)
  day_row <- solar.data[solar.data$date == date, ]
  
  if (nrow(day_row) == 0) return(NA)
  
  sunrise <- as.POSIXct(day_row$sunrise, tz = "Canada/Pacific")
  sunset  <- as.POSIXct(day_row$sunset, tz = "Canada/Pacific")
  
  if (datetime >= sunrise & datetime < sunset) {
    return("day")
  } else {
    return("night")
  }
}

# Determine starting diel period for each interval at t = 0
initial_diel <- zone_intervals_coxPH %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diel_period = get_diel_period(tstart_timestamp, solar.data),
                tchange = 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(interval_id, tchange, diel_period) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Stack sunrise/sunset/dawn/dusk into long format
diel_changes <- solar.data %>%
  dplyr::select(nauticalDawn, sunrise, sunset, nauticalDusk) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "type", values_to = "change_time") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(change_time) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diel_period = ifelse(type == "nauticalDawn", "dawn",
                                     ifelse(type == "sunrise", "day",
                                            ifelse(type == "sunset", "dusk", "night"))))

str(diel_changes)

# Assign each interval an initial diel period
# Function to classify diel period at a given datetime
get_diel_period <- function(datetime, solar.data) {
  date <- as.Date(datetime)
  day_row <- solar.data[solar.data$date == date, ]
  
  if (nrow(day_row) == 0) return(NA)
  
  nauticalDawn <- as.POSIXct(day_row$nauticalDawn, tz = "Canada/Pacific")
  sunrise <- as.POSIXct(day_row$sunrise, tz = "Canada/Pacific")
  sunset  <- as.POSIXct(day_row$sunset, tz = "Canada/Pacific")
  nauticalDusk <- as.POSIXct(day_row$nauticalDusk, tz = "Canada/Pacific")
  
  if (datetime >= nauticalDawn & datetime < sunrise) {
    return("dawn")
  } else if (datetime >= sunrise & datetime < sunset) {
    return("day")
  } else if (datetime >= sunset & datetime < nauticalDusk) {
    return("dusk")
  } else {
    return("night")
  }
}

# Determine starting diel period for each interval at t = 0
initial_diel <- zone_intervals_coxPH %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(diel_period = get_diel_period(tstart_timestamp, solar.data),
                tchange = 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(interval_id, tchange, diel_period) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# Build time-varying events for diel period transitions
diel_events_list <- list()

# Check column types
stopifnot(inherits(zone_intervals_coxPH$tstart_timestamp, "POSIXct"))
stopifnot(inherits(zone_intervals_coxPH$tstop_timestamp, "POSIXct"))
stopifnot(inherits(diel_changes$change_time, "POSIXct"))

diel_events_list <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(zone_intervals_coxPH)) {
  fish <- zone_intervals_coxPH[i, ]
  start <- fish$tstart_timestamp
  stop <- fish$tstop_timestamp
  
  diel_sub <- diel_changes %>%
    dplyr::filter(change_time > start, change_time < stop) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(interval_id = fish$interval_id,
                  tchange = as.numeric(difftime(change_time, start, units = "hours"))) %>%
    dplyr::select(interval_id, tchange, diel_period)
  
  diel_events_list[[i]] <- diel_sub
}

diel_events <- bind_rows(diel_events_list)


# Combine initial diel period and transition events
twilight_events_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(initial_diel, diel_events) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_id, tchange)

# Change the name of the diel_period column to twilight_period

twilight_events_all <- twilight_events_all %>%
  dplyr::select(interval_id, tchange, twilight_period)

# 7. Time-varying river discharge ####

# River discharge data are provided as daily averages
# To incorporate these data as a time-varying covariate, we need to specify Start and End times for each day
# Because there are no specific timestamps associated with the timing of change between discharge values, the Start and End times will be set to 12:00:00 noon for each day. This choice was made based on the knowledge that daily mean values for river discharge are time-weighted averages of 5-minute intervals between 00:00:00 and 23:55:00. However, I should acknowledge that there is the potential for this to influence results in TTE models, since the choice for when to specify the change will influence the exposure of smolts to potentially different discharge rates. This is especially noteworthy if discharge proves to be a highly influential term. Alternatively, I could have it change at 00:00 (midnight) each day. The important consideration is that the choice I make could influence the rate of discharge experienced by each fish at the time of an event, and that this needs to be acknowledged in the study.

flow_data <- discharge.data.2014 %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Time = "12:00:00") %>%
  tidyr::unite(DateTime, Date, Time, sep = " ", remove = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DateTime_Start = as.POSIXct(DateTime),
                DateTime_End = lead(DateTime_Start)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(discharge_m3s = water_flow_m3_s)


flow_events_list <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(zone_intervals_coxPH)) {
  fish <- zone_intervals_coxPH[i, ]
  start <- fish$tstart_timestamp
  stop <- fish$tstop_timestamp
  
  flow_sub <- flow_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(DateTime_End > start, DateTime_Start < stop) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(interval_id = fish$interval_id,
                  tchange = as.numeric(difftime(DateTime_Start, start, units = "hours"))) %>%
    dplyr::select(interval_id, tchange, discharge_m3s)
  
  flow_events_list[[i]] <- flow_sub
}

flow_events_all <- bind_rows(flow_events_list) %>%
  arrange(interval_id, tchange)

# Change all negative values for tchange to 0

flow_events_all <- flow_events_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tchange = if_else(tchange < 0, 0, tchange))


# 8. Time-varying smolt density ####

# We can drastically reduce the number of rows in the final data set if we collapse blocks of sequential 5-min intervals where smolt density = 0
# We just need to make sure we retain the interval start time for the the first 5-min interval and the interval end time for the last 5-min interval
collapsed <- smolt.density.combined %>%
  arrange(DateTime_Start) %>%
  mutate(
    is_zero = smolt_count == 0,
    run_id  = cumsum(is_zero != lag(is_zero, default = !first(is_zero)))
  )

# Rows where smolt_count == 0; collapse by run_id
zero_blocks <- collapsed %>%
  filter(is_zero) %>%
  group_by(run_id) %>%
  summarise(
    DateTime_Start = first(DateTime_Start),
    DateTime_End   = last(DateTime_End),
    smolt_count    = 0L,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Rows where smolt_count > 0; keep as-is
nonzero_rows <- collapsed %>%
  filter(!is_zero) %>%
  dplyr::select(DateTime_Start, DateTime_End, smolt_count)

# Combine zero smolt blocks and non-zero rows
smolt.density.blocked <- bind_rows(zero_blocks, nonzero_rows) %>%
  arrange(DateTime_Start, DateTime_End) %>%
  dplyr::select(-run_id)

# Now, merge smolt counts with zone intervals data
smolt_events_list <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(zone_intervals_coxPH)) {
  fish <- zone_intervals_coxPH[i, ]
  start <- fish$tstart_timestamp
  stop <- fish$tstop_timestamp
  
  smolt_sub <- smolt.density.blocked %>%
    dplyr::filter(DateTime_End > start, DateTime_Start < stop) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(interval_id = fish$interval_id,
                  tchange = as.numeric(difftime(DateTime_Start, start, units = "hours"))) %>%
    dplyr::select(interval_id, tchange, smolt_count)
  
  smolt_events_list[[i]] <- smolt_sub
}

smolt_events_all <- bind_rows(smolt_events_list) %>%
  arrange(interval_id, tchange)

# Change all negative values for tchange to 0
smolt_events_all <- smolt_events_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tchange = if_else(tchange < 0, 0, tchange))


# 9. Build the final data set ####

# To minimize the number of rows in the data set, we collapsed intervals where smolt count was zero for several sequential rows

# We could further minimize the number of rows in each of the zone- and rate-specific data sets by filtering zone intervals first and then adding time-varying covariates for only the covariates of interest for each zone.

# For instance, we could create the data set for cox PH analysis of advancement from the lake to the outlet, which would not include a time-varying covariate for smolt density, thus minimizing the rows in the data set.

# However, we chose to add time-varying covariates to the main cr_cox data and then subset into zone- and rate-specific data sets

# Later, if we want to reduce the number of rows in the zone- and rate-specific data sets, we can remove columns for covariates that are not of interest and collapse intervals where covariate values don't change.   

# Base `tmerge`
tdata1 <- tmerge(data1 = zone_intervals_coxPH,
                 data2 = zone_intervals_coxPH,
                 id = interval_id,
                 event = event(tstop_interval, Zone_next))

# Add fence_status as time-varying covariate
tdata2 <- tmerge(data1 = tdata1,
                 data2 = fence_events_all,
                 id = interval_id,
                 fence_status = tdc(tchange, fence_status))

# Add traps_open as time-varying covariate
tdata3 <- tmerge(data1 = tdata2,
                 data2 = trap_events_all,
                 id = interval_id,
                 traps_open = tdc(tchange, traps_open))

# Add diel_period as time-varying covariate
tdata4 <- tmerge(data1 = tdata3,
                 data2 = diel_events_all,
                 id = interval_id,
                 diel_period = tdc(tchange, diel_period))

# Add twilight_period as time-varying covariate
tdata5 <- tmerge(data1 = tdata4,
                 data2 = twilight_events_all,
                 id = interval_id,
                 twilight_period = tdc(tchange, twilight_period))

# Add discharge_m3s as time-varying covariate
tdata6 <- tmerge(data1 = tdata5,
                 data2 = flow_events_all,
                 id = interval_id,
                 discharge_m3s = tdc(tchange, discharge_m3s))

# Add smolt_density as time-varying covariate
tdata7 <- tmerge(data1 = tdata6,
                 data2 = smolt_events_all,
                 id = interval_id,
                 smolt_count = tdc(tchange, smolt_count))

# The combined data in tdata7 can now be used to construct the cox PH models
cr_cox_data_main <- tdata7

# Ensure covariates are formatted correctly
str(cr_cox_data_main)

cr_cox_data_main$diel_period <- factor(cr_cox_data_main$diel_period, levels = c("day", "night"))

cr_cox_data_main$twilight_period <- factor(cr_cox_data_main$twilight_period, levels = c("day", "dawn", "dusk", "night"))

cr_cox_data_main$traps_open <- factor(cr_cox_data_main$traps_open, levels = c("0", "1", "2"), labels = c("zero", "one", "two"))

# 10. Add time-varying duration of current opening ####

cr_cox_data_main <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Fish_ID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Identify the start of each new open period
    is_new_open_period = fence_status == "open" & lag(fence_status) != "open",
    # Assign a unique ID to each open period (NA when closed)
    open_period_id = dplyr::if_else(fence_status == "open",
                                    cumsum(is_new_open_period),
                                    NA_integer_)
  )

open_period_starts <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::filter(fence_status == "open") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Fish_ID, open_period_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(open_period_start = min(tstart), .groups = "drop")

cr_cox_data_main <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::left_join(open_period_starts, by = c("Fish_ID", "open_period_id")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(duration_current_opening = dplyr::if_else(fence_status == "open",
                                                          as.numeric(tstop - open_period_start), 0))
# 11. Add static covariates ####


# Create a column for release group in the VPS.smolts data
VPS.smolts <- VPS.smolts %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Release_DateTime) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(release_group = as.factor(dplyr::dense_rank(Release_DateTime))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Fish_ID)

# Add static covariates to zone intervals data
foo <- VPS.smolts %>%
  dplyr::select(Fish_ID, FL_mm, Mass_g, Tag_Burden, release_group) %>%
  dplyr::rename(mass_g = Mass_g,
                tag_burden = Tag_Burden) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(K = (mass_g / (FL_mm^3) ) * 100000)

cr_cox_data_main <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::left_join(foo, by = "Fish_ID")

# Arrange cr_cox_data_main by fish ID, tstart_timestamp, and tstart
# The intervals will be ordered chronologically
cr_cox_data_main <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::arrange(Fish_ID, tstart_timestamp, tstart)

# Clean up work space
remove(collapsed, diel_changes, diel_events, diel_events_all, diel_events_list, diel_sub, dt, 
       fence_events_all, fence_events_list, fence_sub, fish, flow_events_all, flow_events_list,
       flow_sub, foo, initial_diel, nonzero_rows, smolt_events_all, smolt_events_list, smolt_sub,
       tdata1, tdata2, tdata3, tdata4, tdata5, tdata6, tdata7, trap_events_all, trap_events_list,
       trap_sub, twilight_events_all, zero_blocks, zone_transitions_list, i, start, 
       stop, build_zone_intervals_from_detections, get_diel_period, save_individual_plots)

# 12. Format & add a Migration date / Season variable ####

cr_cox_data_main <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  tidyr::separate(interval_id, into = c("x", "zone", "zone_interval"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tstart_datetime = tstart_timestamp + (tstart*3600),
                tstop_datetime = tstart_timestamp + (tstop*3600)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(fish_id = Fish_ID,
                zone_next = Zone_next,
                zone_index = zone_interval) %>%
  dplyr::select(fish_id, interval_id, zone, zone_index, zone_next, tstart, tstop, tstart_datetime, tstop_datetime,
                event, fence_status, traps_open, diel_period, twilight_period, discharge_m3s, smolt_count, FL_mm,
                mass_g, K, tag_burden, duration_current_opening, release_group) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(zone_next = if_else(is.na(zone_next), "0", zone_next)) # intervals where zone_next is NA must be censored (last known location)


# Season will be treated as a linear continuous variable representing the number of days since the day prior to the earliest release date.
cr_cox_data_main <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DOY = lubridate::yday(tstart_datetime),
                season_start_temp = min(DOY)-1,
                season = DOY - season_start_temp) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(DOY, season_start_temp))

```

```{r set_up_zone_data_sets, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# Separate main data set into zone- and rate-specific data sets

# As per Alcott et al. 2021, data for competing risk cox PH will be structured such that "When a fish advanced from one zone to the next, that observation was considered complete for the advancing function (Az(t)) and censored for the retreat function (Rz(t)). Conversely, when fish retreated to a previous zone, the observation was complete for calculation of retreat rate and censored for the rate of advance."

# Thus, separate data sets are required to estimate transition rates between adjacent zones
# Because the only possible transition from the lake is advancement, only one data set is required

# Transitions from the Lake zone (Z1) to the Approach zone (Z2)
lake_advance <- cr_cox_data_main %>% 
  dplyr::filter(zone == "Z1") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(event = if_else(event == "2", 1, 0)) # event must be numeric

# Downstream transitions from the Approach zone (Z2) to the Attempt zone (Z3)
outlet_advance <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::filter(zone == "Z2") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(event = if_else(event == "3", 1, 0)) 

# Upstream transitions from the Approach zone (Z2) to the Lake zone (Z1)
outlet_retreat <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::filter(zone == "Z2") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(event = if_else(event == "1", 1, 0)) 

# Downstream transitions from the Attempt zone (Z3) past the fence (Z4)
attempt_advance <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::filter(zone == "Z3") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(event = if_else(event == "4", 1, 0)) 

# Upstream transitions from the Attempt zone (Z3) to the Approach zone (Z2) 
attempt_retreat <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::filter(zone == "Z3") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(event = if_else(event == "2", 1, 0)) 

```

```{r identify_problematic_detections, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# PROBLEMATIC DETECTIONS WERE FILTERED ABOVE
# THUS, THIS CODE WILL NOT IDENTIFY PROBLEMATIC DETECTIONS
# THIS CODE CHUNK JUST ILLUSTRATES HOW THESE DETECTIONS WERE INITIALLY IDENTIFIED 

# For some smolts that passed the fence, passage occurred when the fence was closed
# It's possible these smolts were at the fence before it opened and were primarily detected on DS receivers, and then passed once it opened
# This could cause their passage interval to be recorded as starting just before the fence opened
# Or, they possibly were last detected on downstream receivers without actually passing the fence

# Further, some smolts transitioned directly from Z2 to Z4
# It's likely that these smolts moved quickly through Z3 before passage, and that they were not detected enough for Z3 occupation to be identified

# First, identify the smolts that passed during fence closure, and compare the timing of passage with fence operation and downstream detections

# Smolts that passed fence during a closed period
closed.passage.smolts <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::filter(event == "4" & fence_status == "closed")

closed.passage.smolts.list <- closed.passage.smolts$fish_id

# Filter transitions to zone 4 during periods of fence closure
closed.passage.intervals <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::filter(zone == "Z3" & zone_next == "4") %>%
  dplyr::filter(fish_id %in% closed.passage.smolts.list)

# Seven smolts passed the fence when it was closed
# Four of these smolts were also identified as passing the fence during closure in the combined PIT and VPS cox PH (109, 119, 183, & 231)
# One of these smolts was identified as passing the fence during an open period in the combined data (111)
# Two of these smolts were censored as never passing in the combined data (283 & 293)
# For the combined PIT and acoustic data, which estimated passage of acoustic smolts w/ VPS positions, these smolts were handled as follows:

# 109 - time of fence crossing was changed to May 1 at 02:07:28
# 119 - censored at last observation before passage (May 19 at 21:21:57)
# 183 - censored at last observation before passage (May 15 at 20:53:22)
# 231 - censored at last observation before passage (May 8 at 01:24:57)
# 111 - passed the fence May 1 at 02:07:49
# 283 - censored May 20 at 10:16:31
# 293 - censored May 12 at 13:53:44

# Based on comparison of individual smolt detection histories, fence operation schedule, and downstream detections, these smolts will be handled as follows:

# smolt 109 - censor on 2014-05-01 09:31:43 - no evidence of passage; no downstream detections 
# smolt 119 - censor on 2014-05-19 21:19:00 - no evidence of passage; no downstream detections in freshwater 
# smolt 183 - censor on 2014-05-15 20:47:53 - no evidence of passage, but detected downstream next day; passage likely not detected 
# smolt 231 - change passage timing to 2014-05-09 21:43:44 
# smolt 111 - change passage timing to 2014-05-01 02:07:49
# smolt 283 - censor on 2014-05-20 15:37:20 - no evidence of passage, no downstream detections
# smolt 293 - censor on 2014-05-12 13:54:15 - no evidence of passage; no downstream detections

# For smolts that are censored, discard detections that occur later than the censoring timestamp
# For smolts that passed, discard detections that are flagged as impossible passage
# Discarding detections obviously reduces total detections, but it correctly assigns zone transitions

# Now, identify smolts that skipped Z3 before passage
skipped.Z3.smolts <- cr_cox_data_main %>% 
  dplyr::filter(zone == "Z2" & event == "4")

# smolt 64 - a single detection in Zone 4 (R37) at 2014-05-12 21:42:29 interrupted Zone 3 occupation
# smolt 66 - two detections < 2 minutes apart in Zone 4 (R36 and R35) at 2014-05-13 23:11:34 and 2014-05-13 23:12:28 interrupted Zone 3 occupation
# smolt 85 - two detections < 1 minute apart in Zone 2 (R33 and R10) at 2014-05-14 23:09:30 and 2014-05-14 23:09:50 interrupted Zone 3 occupation

# Make the changes required for smolts that passed the fence during closed periods and for smolts that passed that transitioned directly from Zone 2 in the raw detections before identifying the intervals.

# Make a note documenting why those changes were made, and leave this code as reference.

remove(closed.passage.smolts, closed.passage.smolts.list, closed.passage.intervals, skipped.Z3.smolts)

```

In the code chunks below for each of the zone transitions, user-defined objects can be set in step 1 (SETUP).

The user-defined objects for each of the unique behaviours are currently set to those used for analyses presented in the manuscript.


1. Advancement from the approach zone (Z2) to the attempt zone (Z3)

```{r advancement_cox_PH_frailty, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# Option to fit mixed-effects Cox PH models w/ `coxph` function from `survival` package and w/ frailty term for random effect.

# Only works w/ one level for random effect (i.e., no nested random intercepts)

# 1. SETUP - USER-DEFINED OBJECTS ####

# Re-name the data set
advancement_frailty <- outlet_advance

## Name of the data frame being used for analysis (for setting up analysis-specific directory)
data_name   <- "advancement_frailty"

## Name of the data set (for organizing outputs generated from different data)
dataset_name <- "advancement_frailty"

## Identify the data set being used for analysis
dat <- get(data_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)

# Check levels
table(dat$event, dat$twilight_period)

# Set diel period reference level
levels(dat$twilight_period)
dat$twilight_period <- relevel(dat$twilight_period, ref = "night")

## Time-to-event variables
use_start_stop <- TRUE # TRUE if data set has time-varying covariates (tstart/tstop)
time_var   <- "tstop"   # "tstop" if using start-stop, otherwise "time"
tstart_var <- "tstart"  # only used if use_start_stop = TRUE
status_var <- "event"   # 0/1

## ID for random effect / clustering
id_var <- "fish_id"

## Standardize continuous covariates that might appear in candidate models
dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    z.FL     = as.numeric(scale(FL_mm)),
    z.K      = as.numeric(scale(K)),
    z.season = as.numeric(scale(season))
  )

## List covariates that might appear in models (fixed effects)
fixed_main_covars <- c(
  "z.FL",
  "z.K",
  "z.season",
  "twilight_period"
)

## Identify covariates that are continuous
continuous_covars <- c("z.FL", "z.K", "z.season")

## Continuous covariates (on original scale) that are used for testing the assumption of linearity and to identify extreme outliers
linearity_raw_covars <- c("FL_mm", "K", "season")

## (Optional) covariates that must always be present in any candidate model
#must_have <- c("fence_status") 
must_have <- character(0)

## (Optional) interactions that may be included in candidate models
## (must be specified as "var1:var2" using names from fixed_main_covariates)
interaction_terms <- c("twilight_period:z.season")
# interaction_terms <- character(0) # Use this if interaction terms are not included

## (Optional) interactions that MUST be included whenever their main effects are present
## Must be a subset of interaction_terms.
required_interactions <- c() # e.g., c("twilight_period:z.season")

if (!all(required_interactions %in% interaction_terms)) {
  stop("All required_interactions must also appear in interaction_terms.")
}

## (Optional) covariates that must be used for stratification in every model
# Make sure strata variables are NOT in fixed_main_covars
#strata_covars <- "fence_status"
strata_covars <- character(0)

## (Optional) illegal combinations: lists of covariates that cannot appear in the same model
#never_together <- list(c("z.FL", "z.K")) # High colinearity
never_together <- list() # Use this if illegal combinations do not need to be specified

## Determine the max parameters per model
## Target events-per-variable (EPV) rule (per fixed effect, not counting frailty)
target_epv <- 10L

## Count the number of events in the data
if (!status_var %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("status_var ('", status_var, "') not found in dat.")
}
n_events <- sum(dat[[status_var]] == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)

## Max number of fixed-effect "slots" (main effects + interactions)
max_effects_total <- max(1L, floor(n_events / target_epv))

if (max_effects_total < 3L) {
  warning(
    "Relatively few events (n_events = ", n_events, 
    "); max_effects_total = ", max_effects_total,
    ". Consider simplifying the candidate model set."
  )
}

## Basic counts of what is available
n_main_available <- length(fixed_main_covars)
n_int_available <- length(interaction_terms)
n_must <- length(must_have)

if (n_must > 0L && !all(must_have %in% fixed_main_covars)) {
  stop("All 'must_have' covariates must appear in fixed_main_covars.")
}

## Ensure we can at least include all must-have main effects
if (n_must > max_effects_total) {
  warning(
    "Number of must_have covariates (", n_must, ") exceeds EPV-based max_effects_total (", max_effects_total, ").\n",
    "Forcing max_effects_total = n_must so all must_have terms can be included, ",
    "but this may overfit given the number of events."
  )
  max_effects_total <- n_must
}

## Budget left after forcing must_have main effects
remaining_budget <- max(0L, max_effects_total - n_must)

## Allocate at most half of the non-must budget to interactions
max_interactions <- 0L
if (n_int_available > 0L && remaining_budget > 0L) {
  max_interactions <- min(
    n_int_available,
    floor(remaining_budget / 2L)
  )
}

## Remaining slots go to *additional* main effects beyond must_have
additional_mains <- remaining_budget - max_interactions
max_main_effects <- n_must + min(
  additional_mains,
  max(0L, n_main_available - n_must)
)

message(
  "Events: ", n_events,
  " | target EPV (per fixed effect): ", target_epv,
  " | max_effects_total (main + interaction) = ", max_effects_total,
  "\n  max_main_effects = ", max_main_effects,
  " (including ", n_must, " must_have terms)",
  "\n  max_interactions = ", max_interactions,
  " (frailty(", id_var, ") handled separately)."
)

## Manually set max fixed effects and max number of interactions
## Max number of main effects allowed in any model (excluding interactions)
max_main_effects <- 4

## Maximum number of interactions allowed in any model
max_interactions <- 1

## Parallel computing settings
n_workers <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)
future_globals_maxSize_GB <- 4  # memory ceiling for future (in GB)

## Significance level for PH violations
alpha_ph <- 0.05

## Build Surv() expression as a string
if (!use_start_stop) {
  response_str <- sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var)
} else {
  response_str <- sprintf("Surv(%s, %s, %s)", tstart_var, time_var, status_var)
}

response_formula <- as.formula(paste(response_str, "~ 1"))

# 2. DIRECTORY ####

## Base output directory
base_output_root <- "acoustic_cox_PH_results"

## Main output directory for this run
outdir_root <- file.path(base_output_root, dataset_name)

## Create directory
dir.create(outdir_root, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

message("Main results directory created: ", outdir_root)

## Build directory sub-folders
dir_models    <- file.path(outdir_root, "model_fits")
dir_ph_plots  <- file.path(outdir_root, "ph_plots")
dir_ph_tables <- file.path(outdir_root, "ph_tables")

dir.create(dir_models,    showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_ph_plots,  showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_ph_tables, showWarnings = FALSE)

## Global diagnostics sub-folders
dir_global       <- file.path(outdir_root, "global_diagnostics")
dir_gl_lin       <- file.path(dir_global, "linearity_plots")
dir_gl_influence <- file.path(dir_global, "influence_plots")
dir_gl_tables    <- file.path(dir_global, "tables")

dir.create(dir_global, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_gl_lin,       showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_gl_influence, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_gl_tables,    showWarnings = FALSE)

# 3. DROP IRRELEVANT COLUMNS AND SPLITS ####

## Collapse intervals where covariate values do not change
## And, remove columns not needed for modeling

core_vars <- c(
  id_var,
  status_var,
  time_var,
  if (use_start_stop) tstart_var,
  "interval_id"
)

model_covars <- fixed_main_covars

extra_keep_vars <- c(
  linearity_raw_covars,
  "tstart_datetime",
  "tstop_datetime"
)

keep_vars <- unique(c(core_vars, model_covars, extra_keep_vars))

dat <- dat[, intersect(keep_vars, names(dat))]

if (!"interval_id" %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("interval_id column is required for collapsing but is not present in dat.")
}

collapse_covars <- intersect(model_covars, names(dat))

if ("tstart_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstart_datetime"
} else if ("tstop_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstop_datetime"
} else {
  order_var <- if (use_start_stop) tstart_var else time_var
}

dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data[[order_var]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    across(
      all_of(collapse_covars),
      ~ . != dplyr::lag(.),
      .names = "chg_{.col}"
    ),
    any_cov_change = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1L,
      TRUE,
      {
        chg_mat <- dplyr::across(
          dplyr::starts_with("chg_"),
          ~ ifelse(is.na(.), FALSE, .)
        )
        if (ncol(chg_mat) == 0L) {
          FALSE
        } else {
          rowSums(chg_mat) > 0
        }
      }
    ),
    event_here = .data[[status_var]] == 1L,
    boundary   = any_cov_change | event_here,
    collapse_id = cumsum(boundary)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::starts_with("chg_")) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id, collapse_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    !!sym(tstart_var) := min(.data[[tstart_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(time_var)   := max(.data[[time_var]],   na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(status_var) := max(.data[[status_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = -dplyr::any_of(c("interval_id", "collapse_id",
                               tstart_var, time_var, status_var)),
      .fns  = ~ dplyr::first(.)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(collapse_id, any_cov_change, event_here, boundary)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_id, .data[[tstart_var]])

message("After collapsing within interval_id: ", nrow(dat),
        " rows, ", length(names(dat)), " columns retained.")

# 4. GLOBAL DIAGNOSTICS (LINEARITY & INFLUENCE) ####

## Global model fit with cluster(id_var) --> allowed as global diagnostic
global_formula_str <- paste(
  response_str, "~",
  paste(fixed_main_covars, collapse = " + "),
  "+ cluster(", id_var, ")"
)

global_formula <- as.formula(global_formula_str)

cat("Fitting global coxph model for diagnostics:\n  ", global_formula_str, "\n")
global_fit <- coxph(global_formula, data = dat, ties = "efron")
print(summary(global_fit))

## Linearity checks (unchanged)
for (v in linearity_raw_covars) {
  if (!v %in% names(dat)) {
    warning("Variable '", v, "' not found in dat; skipping linearity check for it.")
    next
  }
  
  form_str <- paste(response_str, "~", v)
  form     <- as.formula(form_str)
  
  fit_v <- coxph(form, data = dat, ties = "efron")
  
  gf_obj <- ggcoxfunctional(
    fit  = fit_v,
    data = dat
  )
  p_lin <- gf_obj[[1]]
  
  outfile <- file.path(dir_gl_lin, paste0("ggcoxfunctional_", v, ".png"))
  ggsave(
    filename = outfile,
    plot     = p_lin,
    width    = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300
  )
  
  message("Saved linearity plot for ", v, " to: ", outfile)
}

message("All ggcoxfunctional linearity plots saved in: ", dir_gl_lin)

## Influence diagnostics (unchanged, based on global_fit)
dfb <- residuals(global_fit, type = "dfbeta") 

coef_names <- names(coef(global_fit))

if (!is.null(coef_names) && length(coef_names) == ncol(dfb)) {
  colnames(dfb) <- coef_names
} else {
  warning(
    "Could not safely map dfbeta columns to coefficient names; ",
    "dfbeta columns will retain their existing names.\n",
    "ncol(dfb) = ", ncol(dfb),
    ", length(coef(global_fit)) = ", length(coef_names)
  )
}

dfb_df <- as.data.frame(dfb)
dfb_df$.row    <- seq_len(nrow(dfb_df))
dfb_df$.id_val <- dat[[id_var]]

dfb_long <- dfb_df %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(.row, .id_val),
    names_to  = "term",
    values_to = "dfbeta"
  )

n_obs <- nrow(dat)
thr   <- 2 / sqrt(n_obs)

dfb_summary <- dfb_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(term) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    max_abs_dfbeta = max(abs(dfbeta), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_above_thr    = sum(abs(dfbeta) > thr, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups        = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(max_abs_dfbeta))

write.csv(
  dfb_summary,
  file.path(dir_gl_tables, "influence_summary_by_term.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

dfb_big <- dfb_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(abs(dfbeta) > thr) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(term, dplyr::desc(abs(dfbeta)))

write.csv(
  dfb_big,
  file.path(dir_gl_tables, "influential_observations.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

for (term_name in unique(dfb_long$term)) {
  sub <- dfb_long %>% dplyr::filter(term == term_name)
  
  x_vals <- sub$.row
  x_lab  <- "Observation index"
  
  plot_df <- tibble::tibble(
    x      = x_vals,
    dfbeta = sub$dfbeta,
    .row   = sub$.row,
    .id_val= sub$.id_val
  )
  
  top_n_label <- 5
  label_df <- plot_df %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(dfbeta))) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = top_n_label)
  
  p_inf <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = dfbeta)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = c(-thr, thr), linetype = "dotted") +
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = label_df,
      ggplot2::aes(label = .id_val),
      vjust = -0.5,
      size  = 3
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title    = paste("Influence diagnostics for term:", term_name),
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Points labelled by ", id_var,
        " (top ", top_n_label, " |dfbeta|)."),
      x = x_lab,
      y = paste("dfbeta (change in log-hazard for", term_name, ")")
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
  
  outfile_inf <- file.path(dir_gl_influence, paste0("dfbeta_", term_name, ".png"))
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = outfile_inf,
    plot     = p_inf,
    width    = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300
  )
  
  message("Saved influence plot for term ", term_name, " to: ", outfile_inf)
}

message("Influence tables saved to: ", dir_gl_tables)
message("Influence plots saved to: ", dir_gl_influence)

diagnostic_only_objects <- c(
  "global_fit",
  "dfb",
  "dfb_df",
  "dfb_long",

  "dfb_big",

)

rm(list = intersect(diagnostic_only_objects, ls()))
message("Clean-up complete: removed diagnostic-only objects. Ready to proceed to model fitting.")

# 5. CANDIDATE MODEL CREATION ####

violates_never_together <- function(vars, never_together) {
  any(vapply(
    never_together,
    function(bad_set) all(bad_set %in% vars),
    logical(1)
  ))
}

build_candidate_formulas <- function(
    fixed_main_covars,
    interaction_terms,
    required_interactions,
    must_have,
    never_together,
    max_main_effects,
    max_interactions,
    response_str,
    id_var,
    strata_covars = character(0)
) {
  ## Ensure these are plain character vectors
  interaction_terms    <- as.character(interaction_terms)
  required_interactions <- as.character(required_interactions)
  
  ## all subsets of main effects
  all_main_subsets <- unlist(
    lapply(seq_along(fixed_main_covars), function(k) {
      combn(fixed_main_covars, k, simplify = FALSE)
    }),
    recursive = FALSE
  )
  
  main_df <- tibble(main_terms = all_main_subsets) %>%
    mutate(
      n_main       = lengths(main_terms),
      has_must     = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ all(must_have %in% .x)),
      violates_bad = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ violates_never_together(.x, never_together))
    ) %>%
    filter(
      n_main <= max_main_effects,
      has_must,
      !violates_bad
    )
  
  ## For each main term set, add interactions that are consistent,
  ## enforcing required_interactions when their main effects are present
  add_interactions <- function(main_terms) {
    ## If there are no candidate interaction terms at all, just return "no interactions"
    if (length(interaction_terms) == 0L) {
      return(list(character(0)))
    }
    
    ## All interactions whose components are in main_terms
    allowed_int_all <- interaction_terms[
      vapply(
        strsplit(interaction_terms, ":", fixed = TRUE),
        function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
        logical(1)
      )
    ]
    
    ## Required interactions for this main term set
    if (length(required_interactions) > 0L) {
      required_int <- required_interactions[
        vapply(
          strsplit(required_interactions, ":", fixed = TRUE),
          function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
          logical(1)
        )
      ]
    } else {
      required_int <- character(0)
    }
    
    ## Optional interactions (allowed but not required)
    optional_int <- setdiff(allowed_int_all, required_int)
    
    ## If the number of required interactions exceeds max_interactions,
    ## this main-term set is not feasible (returns no interaction sets)
    if (length(required_int) > max_interactions) {
      return(list())
    }
    
    ## Always include at least the required interactions
    int_sets <- list(required_int)
    
    if (length(optional_int) == 0L || max_interactions <= length(required_int)) {
      ## No room or no optional interactions
      return(int_sets)
    }
    
    remaining_slots <- max_interactions - length(required_int)
    max_k <- min(remaining_slots, length(optional_int))
    
    for (k in 1:max_k) {
      opt_sets_k <- combn(optional_int, k, simplify = FALSE)
      ## each interaction set is required_int + some optional_int
      opt_sets_k <- lapply(opt_sets_k, function(x) c(required_int, x))
      int_sets   <- c(int_sets, opt_sets_k)
    }
    
    ## Remove possible duplicates of interaction sets
    int_sets_unique <- unique(lapply(int_sets, function(x) sort(as.character(x))))
    int_sets_unique
  }
  
  full_set <- main_df %>%
    mutate(
      interaction_sets = purrr::map(main_terms, add_interactions)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(interaction_sets) %>%
    mutate(
      all_terms     = purrr::map2(main_terms, interaction_sets, c),
      all_terms_chr = purrr::map_chr(all_terms, ~ paste(.x, collapse = " + "))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(all_terms_chr, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(all_terms_chr) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ## build strata() piece, if any
      strata_part = if (length(strata_covars) > 0L) {
        paste0(" + strata(", paste(strata_covars, collapse = ", "), ")")
      } else {
        ""
      },
      ## full coxph formula with frailty
      formula_coxph_chr  = paste0(
        response_str, " ~ ", all_terms_chr,
        strata_part,
        " + frailty(", id_var, ', distribution = "gaussian")'
      )
    )
  
  full_set %>%
    dplyr::select(
      all_terms_chr,  # keep for duplicate checking later
      main_terms,
      interaction_sets,
      all_terms,
      formula_coxph_chr
    )
}

## Build candidate models
candidate_models <- build_candidate_formulas(
  fixed_main_covars     = fixed_main_covars,
  interaction_terms     = interaction_terms,
  required_interactions = required_interactions,
  must_have             = must_have,
  never_together        = never_together,
  max_main_effects      = max_main_effects,
  max_interactions      = max_interactions,
  response_str          = response_str,
  id_var                = id_var,
  strata_covars         = strata_covars
)

## Remove any duplicate formulas and reassign model IDs

candidate_models <- candidate_models %>%
  dplyr::distinct(formula_coxph_chr, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(model_id = paste0("M", dplyr::row_number())) %>%

# 6. FIT CANDIDATE MODELS (coxph + Gaussian frailty & parallel computing) ####

batch_size <- 10 # Batch size for parallel computing

candidate_models <- candidate_models %>%
  dplyr::mutate(batch_id = ceiling(dplyr::row_number() / batch_size))

fit_one_coxph_frailty <- function(row, dat, dir_models) {
  model_id <- row$model_id
  f_coxph  <- as.formula(row$formula_coxph_chr)
  out_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    fit <- readRDS(out_file)
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      coxph(f_coxph, data = dat, ties = "efron"),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    saveRDS(fit, out_file)
  }
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = FALSE,
      logLik     = NA_real_,
      AIC        = NA_real_,
      nparams    = NA_integer_,
      message    = as.character(fit$message)
    )
  } else {
    LL     <- logLik(fit)
    ll_num <- as.numeric(LL)
    df     <- attr(LL, "df")
    aic    <- -2 * ll_num + 2 * df
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = TRUE,
      logLik     = ll_num,
      AIC        = aic,
      nparams    = df,
      message    = NA_character_
    )
  }
}

plan(multisession, workers = n_workers) # Initiate parallel computing

coxph_fit_summary <- candidate_models %>%
  split(.$batch_id) %>%
  purrr::imap_dfr(function(df_batch, b_id) {
    message("Fitting batch ", b_id, " (", nrow(df_batch), " models)")
    future_map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df_batch)), function(i) {
      fit_one_coxph_frailty(df_batch[i, ], dat = dat, dir_models = dir_models)
    })
  })

## Save

# 7. TEST PH ASSUMPTION (coxph + frailty(fish_id)) ####

ph_test_one_model <- function(model_id, dir_models, plot_dir, alpha = 0.05) {
  fit_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (!file.exists(fit_file)) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = "coxph frailty fit file not found"
    ))
  }
  
  fit <- readRDS(fit_file)
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = paste("coxph frailty fit is error object:", fit$message)
    ))
  }
  
  zph <- tryCatch(
    cox.zph(fit),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  
  if (inherits(zph, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = as.character(zph$message)
    ))
  }
  
  plot_file <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(model_id, "_schoenfeld.png"))
  png(plot_file, width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 150)
  par(mfrow = c(ceiling(nrow(zph$table) / 2), 2))
  plot(zph)
  dev.off()
  
  zph_tbl <- as.data.frame(zph$table)
  zph_tbl$term <- rownames(zph_tbl)
  
  zph_tbl <- zph_tbl %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::filter(term != "GLOBAL") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model_id = model_id, .before = 1)
  
  ph_ok <- !any(zph_tbl$p < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  list(
    model_id = model_id,
    ph_ok    = ph_ok,
    zph_tbl  = zph_tbl,
    error    = NA_character_
  )
}

ph_results_list <- future_map(
  candidate_models$model_id,
  ~ ph_test_one_model(.x, dir_models = dir_models, plot_dir = dir_ph_plots, alpha = alpha_ph)
)

ph_tables <- ph_results_list %>%
  purrr::keep(~ !is.null(.x$zph_tbl)) %>%
  purrr::map("zph_tbl") %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows()

)

)

##  11.1: Build list ranked by AIC (MuMIn::model.sel), incl. null frailty model
##  11.2: Subset top models by ΔAIC threshold
##  11.3: Extract coefficients & HRs from top model (plus frailty variance)
##  11.4: Model-averaged coefficients (plus per-model frailty variance)

deltaAIC_threshold <- 2

coxph_fit_summary <- read.csv(out_file_summary)

  dplyr::filter(!is.na(AIC) & is.finite(AIC))

  readRDS(file.path(dir_models, paste0(mid, "_coxph.rds")))
})
names(all_fits) <- model_ids

## 11.1: null model: Surv(...) ~ frailty(fish_id)
null_formula <- as.formula(
  paste0(response_str, " ~ frailty(", id_var, ', distribution = "gaussian")')
)
null_fit <- coxph(null_formula, data = dat, ties = "efron")

null_model_id <- "M0_null"

all_fits_with_null <- c(
  setNames(list(null_fit), null_model_id),
  all_fits
)

models_all <- do.call(
  MuMIn::model.sel,
  c(all_fits_with_null, list(rank = "AIC"))
)

models_all_df$model_id <- rownames(models_all_df)

  dplyr::select(model_id, dplyr::everything()) %>%

## 11.2: Top candidate models (excluding null)
top_models <- subset(
  models_all,
  rownames(models_all) != null_model_id & delta <= deltaAIC_threshold
)

top_models_df <- as.data.frame(top_models)
top_models_df$model_id <- rownames(top_models_df)
top_models_df <- top_models_df %>%
  dplyr::select(model_id, dplyr::everything()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(AIC)

)

    ", excluding null) from MuMIn saved to:\n",
    top_list_file, "\n")


## Helper to extract frailty variance (theta) from coxph
get_frailty_var_coxph <- function(fit) {
  theta <- fit$history$`frailty(fish_id, distribution = "gaussian")`$theta
  if (is.null(theta) || length(theta) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(theta[1])
}

## 11.3: Top model coefficients + frailty variance
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; top-model coefficient table not created.")
} else {
  best_model_name <- rownames(top_models)[1]
  best_fit <- all_fits_with_null[[best_model_name]]
  
  beta <- coef(best_fit)
  vc   <- as.matrix(vcov(best_fit))
  se   <- sqrt(diag(vc))
  
  z_val <- beta / se
  p_val <- 2 * stats::pnorm(abs(z_val), lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  frail_var   <- get_frailty_var_coxph(best_fit)
  frail_sd    <- if (is.na(frail_var)) NA_real_ else sqrt(frail_var)
  
  top_model_coefs <- tibble::tibble(
    term         = names(beta),
    estimate     = as.numeric(beta),
    se           = as.numeric(se),
    z_value      = as.numeric(z_val),
    p_value      = as.numeric(p_val),
    HR           = as.numeric(HR),
    HR_lower_95  = as.numeric(HR_lower_95),
    HR_upper_95  = as.numeric(HR_upper_95),
    model_id     = best_model_name,
    frailty_var  = frail_var,
    frailty_sd   = frail_sd
  )
  
  out_file_top <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_top_model_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    top_model_coefs,
    out_file_top,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Top coxph+frailty model coefficients (with HR, 95% CI, and frailty variance) saved to:\n",
      out_file_top, "\n")
}


## 11.4: Model-averaged coefficients + per-model frailty variance
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; model averaging skipped.")
} else {
  avg_fit <- MuMIn::model.avg(top_models)
  avg_sum <- summary(avg_fit)
  
  avg_coefs <- as.data.frame(avg_sum$coefmat.full)
  avg_coefs$term <- rownames(avg_coefs)
  
  est_col <- "Estimate"
  se_col  <- if ("Std. Error" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "Std. Error"
  } else if ("SE" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "SE"
  } else {
    stop("Could not identify standard error column in avg_coefs.")
  }
  
  beta <- avg_coefs[[est_col]]
  se   <- avg_coefs[[se_col]]
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  avg_coefs$HR          <- HR
  avg_coefs$HR_lower_95 <- HR_lower_95
  avg_coefs$HR_upper_95 <- HR_upper_95
  
  avg_coefs <- avg_coefs %>%
    dplyr::select(
      term,
      dplyr::everything()
    )
  
  out_file_avg <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_model_averaged_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    avg_coefs,
    out_file_avg,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("MuMIn model-averaged coxph+frailty coefficients (with HR and 95% CI) saved to:\n",
      out_file_avg, "\n")
  
  ## Frailty variance for each top model
  top_model_names <- rownames(top_models)
  top_weights     <- top_models$weight
  
  frailty_info <- tibble::tibble(
    model_id = top_model_names,
    weight   = as.numeric(top_weights)
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      frailty_var = vapply(
        model_id,
        function(mid) get_frailty_var_coxph(all_fits_with_null[[mid]]),
        numeric(1)
      ),
      frailty_sd  = ifelse(is.na(frailty_var), NA_real_, sqrt(frailty_var))
    )
  
  out_file_frail <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_frailty_variance_top_models_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    frailty_info,
    out_file_frail,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Frailty variance for each top coxph model (with AIC weights) saved to:\n",
      out_file_frail, "\n")
}


# 12. SUBJECT-SPECIFIC CURVES ####

# Plot subject-specific curves for a hypothetical individual whose covariates are set at user-determined values

# This approach is analogous to predicting covariate effects for other regression models (GLM, GAM,...)
# We set values for the covariates of interest, and hold all other covariates static (often at their mean or median)
# This approach works well for showing the effect size implied by the model coefficients (model-based prediction) and for illustrating interactions, but their weakness is that they represent a hypothetical individual (not the population) and are sensitive to the chosen covariate values, meaning they can be misleading if the chosen covariate profile is unrealistic.  

# Identify the structure of the top model (best_fit), which will be passed to the functions used to create curves:
summary(best_fit)

# 13. MARGINAL (ADJUSTED) CURVES ####


# Marginal curves weren't generated for the manuscript.


# Plot marginal (adjusted) curves that average predictions over the observed covariate distribution

# This approach provides estimates/predictions for a population in which every individual has the same focal value (e.g., diel period. = "night") but all other covariates are left at their original values as they were observed over time.
# This approach removes confounding, provides population-level effects of covariates, and is good for estimating causal effects, but can be more complex to explain, CIs require bootstrapping, and the magnitude of effects is smoothed by averaging (differences between levels of categorical covariates will appear much smaller than the magnitude of difference estimated via hazard ratios)

# Description of this process:
# Instead of creating predictions from a hypothetical “average” fish with all covariates fixed at their mean values, 
# we used a g-computation approach that averages predictions across the actual distribution of all other covariates in the data set.
# In this framework, we intervene only on the covariates of interest (e.g., traps open or season), 
# while leaving every other covariate exactly as observed for each fish. 
# Predicted survival (or cumulative incidence) is generated for every individual under each counterfactual scenario, 
# and these predictions are then averaged to obtain population-level curves.
# This differs from the traditional “hold covariates at their mean” method, 
# which produces predictions for an artificial individual that may not exist and that does not reflect realistic combinations of covariates. 
# The g-computation approach yields curves that are fully adjusted, population-averaged, and interpretable at the ecological scale of interest.

library(riskRegression)
library(adjustedCurves)
library(rlang)

summary(best_fit)

m1 <- coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ z.K + z.season * twilight_period + frailty(fish_id, distribution = "gaussian"), 
            data = dat, 
            x = TRUE, y = TRUE, ties = "efron")

# Prediction function
pred_surv <- function(...) {
  1 - predictRisk(...)
}


# Plot predicted effect of diel period w/out the seasonal effect set manually
# To include CIs, we need to plot bootstrapped estimates

  data          = dat,
  variable      = "twilight_period",  # factor or binary covariate
  ev_time       = "tstop",
  event         = "event",
  method        = "direct",   # standard g-computation
  outcome_model = m1,
  predict_fun   = pred_surv,
  conf_int = TRUE,
  bootstrap = TRUE,
  n_boot = 200
)

                              labels = c("Dawn", "Day", "Dusk", "Night"))

# Write a function that allows CIs to be plotted as steps
make_step_ribbon <- function(df) {
  # df must have columns: time, surv, lower, upper (plus grouping cols)
  df <- df[order(df$time), ]

  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(df)

  # start and end times for each step
  time_start <- df$time
  time_end   <- c(df$time[-1], df$time[nrow(df)])  # last step ends at last time

  # replicate each row twice
  out <- df[rep(seq_len(nrow(df)), each = 2), ]

  # assign stepped times: (t_i, t_{i+1}) for each original row
  out$time <- c(rbind(time_start, time_end))

  out
}

# Update CIs to be plotted as steps

  dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ make_step_ribbon(.x)) %>%
```
