2. Retreat from the approach zone (Z2) to the lake (Z1)

```{r retreat_cox_PH_frailty, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# Option to fit mixed-effects Cox PH models w/ `coxph` function from `survival` pacakge and w/ frailty term for random effect.

# Only works w/ one level for random effect (i.e., no nested random intercepts)

# 1. SETUP - USER-DEFINED OBJECTS ####

# Re-name the data set
retreat_frailty <- outlet_retreat

## Name of the data frame being used for analysis (for setting up analysis-specific directory)
data_name   <- "retreat_frailty"

## Name of the data set (for organizing outputs generated from different data)
dataset_name <- "retreat_frailty"

## Identify the data set being used for analysis
dat <- get(data_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)

# Check levels
table(dat$event, dat$twilight_period)

# Set diel period reference level
levels(dat$twilight_period)
dat$twilight_period <- relevel(dat$twilight_period, ref = "night")

## Time-to-event variables
use_start_stop <- TRUE # TRUE if data set has time-varying covariates (tstart/tstop)
time_var   <- "tstop"   # "tstop" if using start-stop, otherwise "time"
tstart_var <- "tstart"  # only used if use_start_stop = TRUE
status_var <- "event"   # 0/1

## ID for random effect / clustering
id_var <- "fish_id"

## Standardize continuous covariates that might appear in candidate models
dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    z.FL     = as.numeric(scale(FL_mm)),
    z.K      = as.numeric(scale(K)),
    z.season = as.numeric(scale(season))
  )

## Covariates that might appear in models (fixed effects)
fixed_main_covars <- c(
  "z.FL",
  "z.K",
  "z.season",
  "twilight_period"
)

## Which of those covariates are continuous?
continuous_covars <- c("z.FL", "z.K", "z.season")

## Continuous covariates (on original scale) that are used for testing the assumption of linearity and to identify extreme outliers
linearity_raw_covars <- c("FL_mm", "K", "season")

## (Optional) covariates that must always be present in any candidate model
#must_have <- c("fence_status") 
must_have <- character(0)

## (Optional) interactions that may be included in candidate models
## (must be specified as "var1:var2" using names from fixed_main_covariates)
interaction_terms <- c("twilight_period:z.season")
# interaction_terms <- character(0) # Use this if interaction terms are not included

## (Optional) interactions that MUST be included whenever their main effects are present
## Must be a subset of interaction_terms.
required_interactions <- character(0) # e.g., c("twilight_period:z.season")

if (!all(required_interactions %in% interaction_terms)) {
  stop("All required_interactions must also appear in interaction_terms.")
}

## (Optional) covariates that must be used for stratification in every model
# Make sure strata variables are NOT in fixed_main_covars
#strata_covars <- "fence_status"
strata_covars <- character(0)

## (Optional) illegal combinations: lists of covariates that cannot appear in the same model
#never_together <- list(c("z.FL", "z.K")) # High colinearity
never_together <- list() # Use this if illegal combinations do not need to be specified

## Determine the max parameters per model
## Target events-per-variable (EPV) rule (per fixed effect, not counting frailty)
target_epv <- 10L

## Count the number of events in the data
if (!status_var %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("status_var ('", status_var, "') not found in dat.")
}
n_events <- sum(dat[[status_var]] == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)

## Max number of fixed-effect "slots" (main effects + interactions)
max_effects_total <- max(1L, floor(n_events / target_epv))

if (max_effects_total < 3L) {
  warning(
    "Relatively few events (n_events = ", n_events, 
    "); max_effects_total = ", max_effects_total,
    ". Consider simplifying the candidate model set."
  )
}

## Basic counts of what is available
n_main_available <- length(fixed_main_covars)
n_int_available  <- length(interaction_terms)
n_must           <- length(must_have)

if (n_must > 0L && !all(must_have %in% fixed_main_covars)) {
  stop("All 'must_have' covariates must appear in fixed_main_covars.")
}

## Ensure we can at least include all must-have main effects
if (n_must > max_effects_total) {
  warning(
    "Number of must_have covariates (", n_must, 
    ") exceeds EPV-based max_effects_total (", max_effects_total, ").\n",
    "Forcing max_effects_total = n_must so all must_have terms can be included, ",
    "but this may overfit given the number of events."
  )
  max_effects_total <- n_must
}

## Budget left after forcing must_have main effects
remaining_budget <- max(0L, max_effects_total - n_must)

## Allocate at most half of the non-must budget to interactions
max_interactions <- 0L
if (n_int_available > 0L && remaining_budget > 0L) {
  max_interactions <- min(
    n_int_available,
    floor(remaining_budget / 2L)
  )
}

## Remaining slots go to *additional* main effects beyond must_have
additional_mains <- remaining_budget - max_interactions
max_main_effects <- n_must + min(
  additional_mains,
  max(0L, n_main_available - n_must)
)

message(
  "Events: ", n_events,
  " | target EPV (per fixed effect): ", target_epv,
  " | max_effects_total (main + interaction) = ", max_effects_total,
  "\n  max_main_effects = ", max_main_effects,
  " (including ", n_must, " must_have terms)",
  "\n  max_interactions = ", max_interactions,
  " (frailty(", id_var, ") handled separately)."
)

## Manually set max fixed effects and max number of interactions
## Max number of main effects allowed in any model (excluding interactions)
max_main_effects <- 4

## Maximum number of interactions allowed in any model
max_interactions <- 1

## Parallel computing settings

future_globals_maxSize_GB <- 4  # memory ceiling for future (in GB)

)

  linearity_raw_covars,
  "tstart_datetime",
  "tstop_datetime"
)

dat <- dat[, intersect(keep_vars, names(dat))]

if (!"interval_id" %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("interval_id column is required for collapsing but is not present in dat.")
}

collapse_covars <- intersect(model_covars, names(dat))

if ("tstart_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstart_datetime"
} else if ("tstop_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstop_datetime"
} else {
  order_var <- if (use_start_stop) tstart_var else time_var
}

dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data[[order_var]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    across(
      all_of(collapse_covars),
      ~ . != dplyr::lag(.),
      .names = "chg_{.col}"
    ),
    any_cov_change = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1L,
      TRUE,
      {
        chg_mat <- dplyr::across(
          dplyr::starts_with("chg_"),
          ~ ifelse(is.na(.), FALSE, .)
        )
        if (ncol(chg_mat) == 0L) {
          FALSE
        } else {
          rowSums(chg_mat) > 0
        }
      }
    ),
    event_here = .data[[status_var]] == 1L,
    boundary   = any_cov_change | event_here,
    collapse_id = cumsum(boundary)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::starts_with("chg_")) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id, collapse_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    !!sym(tstart_var) := min(.data[[tstart_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(time_var)   := max(.data[[time_var]],   na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(status_var) := max(.data[[status_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = -dplyr::any_of(c("interval_id", "collapse_id",
                               tstart_var, time_var, status_var)),
      .fns  = ~ dplyr::first(.)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(collapse_id, any_cov_change, event_here, boundary)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_id, .data[[tstart_var]])

# 5. CANDIDATE MODEL CREATION ####

violates_never_together <- function(vars, never_together) {
  any(vapply(
    never_together,
    function(bad_set) all(bad_set %in% vars),
    logical(1)
  ))
}

build_candidate_formulas <- function(
    fixed_main_covars,
    interaction_terms,
    required_interactions,
    must_have,
    never_together,
    max_main_effects,
    max_interactions,
    response_str,
    id_var,
    strata_covars = character(0)
) {
  ## Ensure these are plain character vectors
  interaction_terms    <- as.character(interaction_terms)
  required_interactions <- as.character(required_interactions)
  
  ## all subsets of main effects
  all_main_subsets <- unlist(
    lapply(seq_along(fixed_main_covars), function(k) {
      combn(fixed_main_covars, k, simplify = FALSE)
    }),
    recursive = FALSE
  )
  
  main_df <- tibble(main_terms = all_main_subsets) %>%
    mutate(
      n_main       = lengths(main_terms),
      has_must     = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ all(must_have %in% .x)),
      violates_bad = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ violates_never_together(.x, never_together))
    ) %>%
    filter(
      n_main <= max_main_effects,
      has_must,
      !violates_bad
    )
  
  ## For each main term set, add interactions that are consistent,
  ## enforcing required_interactions when their main effects are present
  add_interactions <- function(main_terms) {
    ## If there are no candidate interaction terms at all, just return "no interactions"
    if (length(interaction_terms) == 0L) {
      return(list(character(0)))
    }
    
    ## All interactions whose components are in main_terms
    allowed_int_all <- interaction_terms[
      vapply(
        strsplit(interaction_terms, ":", fixed = TRUE),
        function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
        logical(1)
      )
    ]
    
    ## Required interactions for this main term set
    if (length(required_interactions) > 0L) {
      required_int <- required_interactions[
        vapply(
          strsplit(required_interactions, ":", fixed = TRUE),
          function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
          logical(1)
        )
      ]
    } else {
      required_int <- character(0)
    }
    
    ## Optional interactions (allowed but not required)
    optional_int <- setdiff(allowed_int_all, required_int)
    
    ## If the number of required interactions exceeds max_interactions,
    ## this main-term set is not feasible (returns no interaction sets)
    if (length(required_int) > max_interactions) {
      return(list())
    }
    
    ## Always include at least the required interactions
    int_sets <- list(required_int)
    
    if (length(optional_int) == 0L || max_interactions <= length(required_int)) {
      ## No room or no optional interactions
      return(int_sets)
    }
    
    remaining_slots <- max_interactions - length(required_int)
    max_k <- min(remaining_slots, length(optional_int))
    
    for (k in 1:max_k) {
      opt_sets_k <- combn(optional_int, k, simplify = FALSE)
      ## each interaction set is required_int + some optional_int
      opt_sets_k <- lapply(opt_sets_k, function(x) c(required_int, x))
      int_sets   <- c(int_sets, opt_sets_k)
    }
    
    ## Remove possible duplicates of interaction sets
    int_sets_unique <- unique(lapply(int_sets, function(x) sort(as.character(x))))
    int_sets_unique
  }
  
  full_set <- main_df %>%
    mutate(
      interaction_sets = purrr::map(main_terms, add_interactions)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(interaction_sets) %>%
    mutate(
      all_terms     = purrr::map2(main_terms, interaction_sets, c),
      all_terms_chr = purrr::map_chr(all_terms, ~ paste(.x, collapse = " + "))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(all_terms_chr, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(all_terms_chr) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ## build strata() piece, if any
      strata_part = if (length(strata_covars) > 0L) {
        paste0(" + strata(", paste(strata_covars, collapse = ", "), ")")
      } else {
        ""
      },
      ## full coxph formula with frailty
      formula_coxph_chr  = paste0(
        response_str, " ~ ", all_terms_chr,
        strata_part,
        " + frailty(", id_var, ', distribution = "gaussian")'
      )
    )
  
  full_set %>%
    dplyr::select(
      all_terms_chr,  # keep for duplicate checking later
      main_terms,
      interaction_sets,
      all_terms,
      formula_coxph_chr
    )
}

## Build candidate models
candidate_models <- build_candidate_formulas(
  fixed_main_covars     = fixed_main_covars,
  interaction_terms     = interaction_terms,
  required_interactions = required_interactions,
  must_have             = must_have,
  never_together        = never_together,
  max_main_effects      = max_main_effects,
  max_interactions      = max_interactions,
  response_str          = response_str,
  id_var                = id_var,
  strata_covars         = strata_covars
)

## Remove any duplicate formulas and reassign model IDs
n_before <- nrow(candidate_models)
candidate_models <- candidate_models %>%
  dplyr::distinct(formula_coxph_chr, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(model_id = paste0("M", dplyr::row_number())) %>%
  dplyr::relocate(model_id, .before = 1)

n_after <- nrow(candidate_models)
if (n_after < n_before) {

}

batch_size <- 10

  dplyr::mutate(batch_id = ceiling(dplyr::row_number() / batch_size))

fit_one_coxph_frailty <- function(row, dat, dir_models) {
  model_id <- row$model_id
  f_coxph  <- as.formula(row$formula_coxph_chr)
  out_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    fit <- readRDS(out_file)
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      coxph(f_coxph, data = dat, ties = "efron"),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    saveRDS(fit, out_file)
  }
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = FALSE,
      logLik     = NA_real_,
      AIC        = NA_real_,
      nparams    = NA_integer_,
      message    = as.character(fit$message)
    )
  } else {
    LL     <- logLik(fit)
    ll_num <- as.numeric(LL)
    df     <- attr(LL, "df")
    aic    <- -2 * ll_num + 2 * df
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = TRUE,
      logLik     = ll_num,
      AIC        = aic,
      nparams    = df,
      message    = NA_character_
    )
  }
}

plan(multisession, workers = n_workers)

coxph_fit_summary <- candidate_models %>%
  split(.$batch_id) %>%
  purrr::imap_dfr(function(df_batch, b_id) {
    message("Fitting batch ", b_id, " (", nrow(df_batch), " models)")
    future_map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df_batch)), function(i) {
      fit_one_coxph_frailty(df_batch[i, ], dat = dat, dir_models = dir_models)
    })
  })

# 7. TEST PH ASSUMPTION (coxph + frailty(fish_id)) ####

ph_test_one_model <- function(model_id, dir_models, plot_dir, alpha = 0.05) {
  fit_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (!file.exists(fit_file)) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = "coxph frailty fit file not found"
    ))
  }
  
  fit <- readRDS(fit_file)
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = paste("coxph frailty fit is error object:", fit$message)
    ))
  }
  
  zph <- tryCatch(
    cox.zph(fit),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  
  if (inherits(zph, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = as.character(zph$message)
    ))
  }
  
  plot_file <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(model_id, "_schoenfeld.png"))
  png(plot_file, width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 150)
  par(mfrow = c(ceiling(nrow(zph$table) / 2), 2))
  plot(zph)
  dev.off()
  
  zph_tbl <- as.data.frame(zph$table)
  zph_tbl$term <- rownames(zph_tbl)
  
  zph_tbl <- zph_tbl %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::filter(term != "GLOBAL") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model_id = model_id, .before = 1)
  
  ph_ok <- !any(zph_tbl$p < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  list(
    model_id = model_id,
    ph_ok    = ph_ok,
    zph_tbl  = zph_tbl,
    error    = NA_character_
  )
}

ph_results_list <- future_map(

          n_after, " unique models remain.")
}

batch_size <- 10

candidate_models <- candidate_models %>%
  dplyr::mutate(batch_id = ceiling(dplyr::row_number() / batch_size))

fit_one_coxph_frailty <- function(row, dat, dir_models) {
  model_id <- row$model_id
  f_coxph  <- as.formula(row$formula_coxph_chr)
  out_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    fit <- readRDS(out_file)
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      coxph(f_coxph, data = dat, ties = "efron"),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    saveRDS(fit, out_file)
  }
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      formula    = row$formula_coxph_chr,
      logLik     = NA_real_,
      AIC        = NA_real_,
      deltaAIC   = NA_real_,
      weight     = NA_real_,
      nparams    = NA_integer_,
      message    = as.character(fit$message)
    )
  } else {
    LL     <- logLik(fit)
    ll_num <- as.numeric(LL)
    df     <- attr(LL, "df")
    aic    <- -2 * ll_num + 2 * df
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      formula    = row$formula_coxph_chr,
      logLik     = ll_num,
      AIC        = aic,
      deltaAIC   = NA_real_,
      weight     = NA_real_,
      nparams    = df,
      message    = NA_character_
    )
  }
}

plan(multisession, workers = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))

coxph_fit_summary <- candidate_models %>%

  purrr::imap_dfr(function(df_batch, b_id) {
    message("Refitting batch ", b_id, " (", nrow(df_batch), " models)")
    future_map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df_batch)), function(i) {
      fit_one_coxph_frailty(df_batch[i, ], dat = dat, dir_models = dir_models)
    })
  })

# 11. MODEL AVERAGING ####
##  11.1: Build list ranked by AIC (MuMIn::model.sel), incl. null frailty model
##  11.2: Subset top models by ΔAIC threshold
##  11.3: Extract coefficients & HRs from top model (plus frailty variance)
##  11.4: Model-averaged coefficients (plus per-model frailty variance)

deltaAIC_threshold <- 2

coxph_fit_summary <- read.csv(out_file_summary)

  dplyr::filter(!is.na(AIC) & is.finite(AIC))

  readRDS(file.path(dir_models, paste0(mid, "_coxph.rds")))
})
names(all_fits) <- model_ids

## 11.1: null model: Surv(...) ~ frailty(fish_id)
null_formula <- as.formula(
  paste0(response_str, " ~ frailty(", id_var, ', distribution = "gaussian")')
)
null_fit <- coxph(null_formula, data = dat, ties = "efron")

null_model_id <- "M0_null"

all_fits_with_null <- c(
  setNames(list(null_fit), null_model_id),
  all_fits
)

models_all <- do.call(
  MuMIn::model.sel,
  c(all_fits_with_null, list(rank = "AIC"))
)

## 11.2: Top candidate models (excluding null)
top_models <- subset(
  models_all,
  rownames(models_all) != null_model_id & delta <= deltaAIC_threshold
)

top_models_df <- as.data.frame(top_models)
top_models_df$model_id <- rownames(top_models_df)

  dplyr::select(model_id, dplyr::everything()) %>%

)

    ", excluding null) from MuMIn saved to:\n",
    top_list_file, "\n")


## Helper to extract frailty variance (theta) from coxph
get_frailty_var_coxph <- function(fit) {
  theta <- fit$history$`frailty(fish_id, distribution = "gaussian")`$theta
  if (is.null(theta) || length(theta) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(theta[1])
}

## 11.3: Top model coefficients + frailty variance
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; top-model coefficient table not created.")
} else {
  best_model_name <- rownames(top_models)[1]
  best_fit <- all_fits_with_null[[best_model_name]]
  
  beta <- coef(best_fit)
  vc   <- as.matrix(vcov(best_fit))
  se   <- sqrt(diag(vc))
  
  z_val <- beta / se
  p_val <- 2 * stats::pnorm(abs(z_val), lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  frail_var   <- get_frailty_var_coxph(best_fit)
  frail_sd    <- if (is.na(frail_var)) NA_real_ else sqrt(frail_var)
  
  top_model_coefs <- tibble::tibble(
    term         = names(beta),
    estimate     = as.numeric(beta),
    se           = as.numeric(se),
    z_value      = as.numeric(z_val),
    p_value      = as.numeric(p_val),
    HR           = as.numeric(HR),
    HR_lower_95  = as.numeric(HR_lower_95),
    HR_upper_95  = as.numeric(HR_upper_95),
    model_id     = best_model_name,
    frailty_var  = frail_var,
    frailty_sd   = frail_sd
  )
  
  out_file_top <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_top_model_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    top_model_coefs,
    out_file_top,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Top coxph+frailty model coefficients (with HR, 95% CI, and frailty variance) saved to:\n",
      out_file_top, "\n")
}


## 11.4: Model-averaged coefficients + per-model frailty variance
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; model averaging skipped.")
} else {
  avg_fit <- MuMIn::model.avg(top_models)
  avg_sum <- summary(avg_fit)
  
  avg_coefs <- as.data.frame(avg_sum$coefmat.full)
  avg_coefs$term <- rownames(avg_coefs)
  
  est_col <- "Estimate"
  se_col  <- if ("Std. Error" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "Std. Error"
  } else if ("SE" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "SE"
  } else {
    stop("Could not identify standard error column in avg_coefs.")
  }
  
  beta <- avg_coefs[[est_col]]
  se   <- avg_coefs[[se_col]]
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  avg_coefs$HR          <- HR
  avg_coefs$HR_lower_95 <- HR_lower_95
  avg_coefs$HR_upper_95 <- HR_upper_95
  
  avg_coefs <- avg_coefs %>%
    dplyr::select(
      term,
      dplyr::everything()
    )
  
  out_file_avg <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_model_averaged_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    avg_coefs,
    out_file_avg,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("MuMIn model-averaged coxph+frailty coefficients (with HR and 95% CI) saved to:\n",
      out_file_avg, "\n")
  
  ## Frailty variance for each top model
  top_model_names <- rownames(top_models)
  top_weights     <- top_models$weight
  
  frailty_info <- tibble::tibble(
    model_id = top_model_names,
    weight   = as.numeric(top_weights)
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      frailty_var = vapply(
        model_id,
        function(mid) get_frailty_var_coxph(all_fits_with_null[[mid]]),
        numeric(1)
      ),
      frailty_sd  = ifelse(is.na(frailty_var), NA_real_, sqrt(frailty_var))
    )
  
  out_file_frail <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_frailty_variance_top_models_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    frailty_info,
    out_file_frail,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Frailty variance for each top coxph model (with AIC weights) saved to:\n",
      out_file_frail, "\n")
}

# 13. MARGINAL (ADJUSTED) CURVES ####

# Plot marginal (adjusted) curves that average predictions over the observed covariate distribution

# This approach provides estimates/predictions for a population in which everyone has the same focal value (e.g., diel period. = "night") but all other covariates are left at their original, observed values.
# This approach removes confounding, provides population-level effect of covariates, and is good for estimating causal effects, but can be more complex to explain, CIs require bootstrapping, and the magnitude of effects is smoothed by averaging.

# Description of this process (e.g., for manuscript):
# Instead of creating predictions from a hypothetical “average” fish with all covariates fixed at their mean values, 
# we used a g-computation approach that averages predictions across the actual distribution of all other covariates in the data set.
# In this framework, we intervene only on the covariates of interest (e.g., traps open or season), 
# while leaving every other covariate exactly as observed for each fish. 
# Predicted survival (or cumulative incidence) is generated for every individual under each counterfactual scenario, 
# and these predictions are then averaged to obtain population-level curves.
# This differs from the traditional “hold covariates at their mean” method, 
# which produces predictions for an artificial individual that may not exist and that does not reflect realistic combinations of covariates. 
# The g-computation approach yields curves that are fully adjusted, population-averaged, and interpretable at the ecological scale of interest.

library(riskRegression)
library(adjustedCurves)
library(rlang)

summary(best_fit)

m1 <- coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ z.FL + z.season * twilight_period + frailty(fish_id, distribution = "gaussian"), 
            data = dat, 
            x = TRUE, y = TRUE, ties = "efron")

# Prediction function
pred_surv <- function(...) {
  1 - predictRisk(...)
}

# Plot predicted effect of diel period w/out the seasonal effect set manually
# To include CIs, we need to plot bootstrapped estimates

  data          = dat,
  variable      = "twilight_period",  # factor or binary covariate
  ev_time       = "tstop",
  event         = "event",
  method        = "direct",   # standard g-computation
  outcome_model = m1,
  predict_fun   = pred_surv,
  conf_int = TRUE,
  bootstrap = TRUE,
  n_boot = 200
)

# Re-order diel period levels

plot_dat_boot$group <- factor(plot_dat_boot$group, levels = c("dawn", "day", "dusk", "night"), 
                              labels = c("Dawn", "Day", "Dusk", "Night"))

# Write a function that allows CIs to be plotted as steps
make_step_ribbon <- function(df) {
  # df must have columns: time, surv, lower, upper (plus grouping cols)
  df <- df[order(df$time), ]

  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(df)

  # start and end times for each step
  time_start <- df$time
  time_end   <- c(df$time[-1], df$time[nrow(df)])  # last step ends at last time

  # replicate each row twice
  out <- df[rep(seq_len(nrow(df)), each = 2), ]

  # assign stepped times: (t_i, t_{i+1}) for each original row
  out$time <- c(rbind(time_start, time_end))

  out
}

# Update CIs to be plotted as steps
plot_dat_step <- plot_dat_boot %>%
  dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ make_step_ribbon(.x)) %>%
```

3. Re-entry from the lake (Z1) to the approach zone (Z2)

```{r re-entry_cox_PH_frailty, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# Option to fit mixed-effects Cox PH models w/ `coxph` function from `survival` package and w/ frailty term for random effect.

# Only works w/ one level for random effect (i.e., no nested random intercepts)

# 1. SETUP - USER-DEFINED OBJECTS ####

# Re-name the data set
re_entry_frailty <- lake_advance

## Name of the data frame being used for analysis (for setting up analysis-specific directory)
data_name   <- "re_entry_frailty"

## Name of the data set (for organizing outputs generated from different data)
dataset_name <- "re_entry_frailty"

## Identify the data set being used for analysis
dat <- get(data_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)

# Check levels
table(dat$event, dat$twilight_period)

# Set diel period reference level
levels(dat$twilight_period)
dat$twilight_period <- relevel(dat$twilight_period, ref = "night")

## Time-to-event variables
use_start_stop <- TRUE # TRUE if data set has time-varying covariates (tstart/tstop)
time_var   <- "tstop"   # "tstop" if using start-stop, otherwise "time"
tstart_var <- "tstart"  # only used if use_start_stop = TRUE
status_var <- "event"   # 0/1

## ID for random effect / clustering
id_var <- "fish_id"

## Standardize continuous covariates that might appear in candidate models
dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    z.FL     = as.numeric(scale(FL_mm)),
    z.K      = as.numeric(scale(K)),
    z.season = as.numeric(scale(season))
  )

## Covariates that might appear in models (fixed effects)
fixed_main_covars <- c(
  "z.FL",
  "z.K",
  "z.season",
  "twilight_period"
)

## Which of those covariates are continuous?
continuous_covars <- c("z.FL", "z.K", "z.season")

## Continuous covariates (on original scale) that are used for testing the assumption of linearity and to identify extreme outliers
linearity_raw_covars <- c("FL_mm", "K", "season")

## (Optional) covariates that must always be present in any candidate model
#must_have <- c("fence_status") 
must_have <- character(0)

## (Optional) interactions that may be included in candidate models
## (must be specified as "var1:var2" using names from fixed_main_covariates)
interaction_terms <- c("twilight_period:z.season")
# interaction_terms <- character(0) # Use this if interaction terms are not included

## (Optional) interactions that MUST be included whenever their main effects are present
## Must be a subset of interaction_terms.
required_interactions <- character(0) # e.g., c("twilight_period:z.season")

if (!all(required_interactions %in% interaction_terms)) {
  stop("All required_interactions must also appear in interaction_terms.")
}

## (Optional) covariates that must be used for stratification in every model
# Make sure strata variables are NOT in fixed_main_covars
#strata_covars <- "fence_status"
strata_covars <- character(0)

## (Optional) illegal combinations: lists of covariates that cannot appear in the same model
#never_together <- list(c("z.FL", "z.K")) # High colinearity
never_together <- list() # Use this if illegal combinations do not need to be specified

## Determine the max parameters per model
## Target events-per-variable (EPV) rule (per fixed effect, not counting frailty)
target_epv <- 10L

## Count the number of events in the data
if (!status_var %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("status_var ('", status_var, "') not found in dat.")
}
n_events <- sum(dat[[status_var]] == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)

## Max number of fixed-effect "slots" (main effects + interactions)
max_effects_total <- max(1L, floor(n_events / target_epv))

if (max_effects_total < 3L) {
  warning(
    "Relatively few events (n_events = ", n_events, 
    "); max_effects_total = ", max_effects_total,
    ". Consider simplifying the candidate model set."
  )
}

## Basic counts of what is available
n_main_available <- length(fixed_main_covars)
n_int_available  <- length(interaction_terms)
n_must           <- length(must_have)

if (n_must > 0L && !all(must_have %in% fixed_main_covars)) {
  stop("All 'must_have' covariates must appear in fixed_main_covars.")
}

## Ensure we can at least include all must-have main effects
if (n_must > max_effects_total) {
  warning(
    "Number of must_have covariates (", n_must, 
    ") exceeds EPV-based max_effects_total (", max_effects_total, ").\n",
    "Forcing max_effects_total = n_must so all must_have terms can be included, ",
    "but this may overfit given the number of events."
  )
  max_effects_total <- n_must
}

## Budget left after forcing must_have main effects
remaining_budget <- max(0L, max_effects_total - n_must)

## Allocate at most half of the non-must budget to interactions
max_interactions <- 0L
if (n_int_available > 0L && remaining_budget > 0L) {
  max_interactions <- min(
    n_int_available,
    floor(remaining_budget / 2L)
  )
}

## Remaining slots go to *additional* main effects beyond must_have
additional_mains <- remaining_budget - max_interactions
max_main_effects <- n_must + min(
  additional_mains,
  max(0L, n_main_available - n_must)
)

message(
  "Events: ", n_events,
  " | target EPV (per fixed effect): ", target_epv,
  " | max_effects_total (main + interaction) = ", max_effects_total,
  "\n  max_main_effects = ", max_main_effects,
  " (including ", n_must, " must_have terms)",
  "\n  max_interactions = ", max_interactions,
  " (frailty(", id_var, ") handled separately)."
)

## Manually set max fixed effects and max number of interactions
## Max number of main effects allowed in any model (excluding interactions)
max_main_effects <- 4

## Maximum number of interactions allowed in any model
max_interactions <- 1

## Parallel computing settings
n_workers <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)
future_globals_maxSize_GB <- 4  # memory ceiling for future (in GB)

## Significance level for PH violations
alpha_ph <- 0.05

## Build Surv() expression as a string
if (!use_start_stop) {
  response_str <- sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var)
} else {
  response_str <- sprintf("Surv(%s, %s, %s)", tstart_var, time_var, status_var)
}

response_formula <- as.formula(paste(response_str, "~ 1"))

# 2. DIRECTORY ####

## Base output directory
base_output_root <- "acoustic_cox_PH_results"

## Main output directory for this run
outdir_root <- file.path(base_output_root, dataset_name)

## Create directory
dir.create(outdir_root, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

message("Main results directory created: ", outdir_root)

## Build directory sub-folders
dir_models    <- file.path(outdir_root, "model_fits")
dir_ph_plots  <- file.path(outdir_root, "ph_plots")
dir_ph_tables <- file.path(outdir_root, "ph_tables")

dir.create(dir_models,    showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_ph_plots,  showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_ph_tables, showWarnings = FALSE)

## Global diagnostics sub-folders
dir_global       <- file.path(outdir_root, "global_diagnostics")
dir_gl_lin       <- file.path(dir_global, "linearity_plots")
dir_gl_influence <- file.path(dir_global, "influence_plots")
dir_gl_tables    <- file.path(dir_global, "tables")

dir.create(dir_global, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_gl_lin,       showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_gl_influence, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_gl_tables,    showWarnings = FALSE)

# 3. DROP IRRELEVANT COLUMNS AND SPLITS ####

## Collapse intervals where covariate values do not change
## And, remove columns not needed for modeling

core_vars <- c(
  id_var,
  status_var,
  time_var,
  if (use_start_stop) tstart_var,
  "interval_id"
)

model_covars <- fixed_main_covars

extra_keep_vars <- c(
  linearity_raw_covars,
  "tstart_datetime",
  "tstop_datetime"
)

keep_vars <- unique(c(core_vars, model_covars, extra_keep_vars))

dat <- dat[, intersect(keep_vars, names(dat))]

if (!"interval_id" %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("interval_id column is required for collapsing but is not present in dat.")
}

collapse_covars <- intersect(model_covars, names(dat))

if ("tstart_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstart_datetime"
} else if ("tstop_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstop_datetime"
} else {
  order_var <- if (use_start_stop) tstart_var else time_var
}

dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data[[order_var]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    across(
      all_of(collapse_covars),
      ~ . != dplyr::lag(.),
      .names = "chg_{.col}"
    ),
    any_cov_change = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1L,
      TRUE,
      {
        chg_mat <- dplyr::across(
          dplyr::starts_with("chg_"),
          ~ ifelse(is.na(.), FALSE, .)
        )
        if (ncol(chg_mat) == 0L) {
          FALSE
        } else {
          rowSums(chg_mat) > 0
        }
      }
    ),
    event_here = .data[[status_var]] == 1L,
    boundary   = any_cov_change | event_here,
    collapse_id = cumsum(boundary)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::starts_with("chg_")) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id, collapse_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    !!sym(tstart_var) := min(.data[[tstart_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(time_var)   := max(.data[[time_var]],   na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(status_var) := max(.data[[status_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = -dplyr::any_of(c("interval_id", "collapse_id",
                               tstart_var, time_var, status_var)),
      .fns  = ~ dplyr::first(.)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(collapse_id, any_cov_change, event_here, boundary)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_id, .data[[tstart_var]])

message("After collapsing within interval_id: ", nrow(dat),
        " rows, ", length(names(dat)), " columns retained.")

# 4. GLOBAL DIAGNOSTICS (LINEARITY & INFLUENCE) ####

## Global model fit with cluster(id_var) --> allowed as global diagnostic
global_formula_str <- paste(
  response_str, "~",
  paste(fixed_main_covars, collapse = " + "),
  "+ cluster(", id_var, ")"
)

global_formula <- as.formula(global_formula_str)

cat("Fitting global coxph model for diagnostics:\n  ", global_formula_str, "\n")
global_fit <- coxph(global_formula, data = dat, ties = "efron")
print(summary(global_fit))

## Linearity checks (unchanged)
for (v in linearity_raw_covars) {
  if (!v %in% names(dat)) {
    warning("Variable '", v, "' not found in dat; skipping linearity check for it.")
    next
  }
  
  form_str <- paste(response_str, "~", v)
  form     <- as.formula(form_str)
  
  fit_v <- coxph(form, data = dat, ties = "efron")
  
  gf_obj <- ggcoxfunctional(
    fit  = fit_v,
    data = dat
  )
  p_lin <- gf_obj[[1]]
  
  outfile <- file.path(dir_gl_lin, paste0("ggcoxfunctional_", v, ".png"))
  ggsave(
    filename = outfile,
    plot     = p_lin,
    width    = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300
  )
  
  message("Saved linearity plot for ", v, " to: ", outfile)
}

message("All ggcoxfunctional linearity plots saved in: ", dir_gl_lin)

## Influence diagnostics (unchanged, based on global_fit)
dfb <- residuals(global_fit, type = "dfbeta") 

coef_names <- names(coef(global_fit))

if (!is.null(coef_names) && length(coef_names) == ncol(dfb)) {
  colnames(dfb) <- coef_names
} else {
  warning(
    "Could not safely map dfbeta columns to coefficient names; ",
    "dfbeta columns will retain their existing names.\n",
    "ncol(dfb) = ", ncol(dfb),
    ", length(coef(global_fit)) = ", length(coef_names)
  )
}

dfb_df <- as.data.frame(dfb)
dfb_df$.row    <- seq_len(nrow(dfb_df))
dfb_df$.id_val <- dat[[id_var]]

dfb_long <- dfb_df %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(.row, .id_val),
    names_to  = "term",
    values_to = "dfbeta"
  )

n_obs <- nrow(dat)
thr   <- 2 / sqrt(n_obs)

dfb_summary <- dfb_long %>%
  dplyr::group_by(term) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    max_abs_dfbeta = max(abs(dfbeta), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_above_thr    = sum(abs(dfbeta) > thr, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups        = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(max_abs_dfbeta))

write.csv(
  dfb_summary,
  file.path(dir_gl_tables, "influence_summary_by_term.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

dfb_big <- dfb_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(abs(dfbeta) > thr) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(term, dplyr::desc(abs(dfbeta)))

write.csv(
  dfb_big,
  file.path(dir_gl_tables, "influential_observations.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

for (term_name in unique(dfb_long$term)) {
  sub <- dfb_long %>% dplyr::filter(term == term_name)
  
  x_vals <- sub$.row
  x_lab  <- "Observation index"
  
  plot_df <- tibble::tibble(
    x      = x_vals,
    dfbeta = sub$dfbeta,
    .row   = sub$.row,
    .id_val= sub$.id_val
  )
  
  top_n_label <- 5
  label_df <- plot_df %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(dfbeta))) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = top_n_label)
  
  p_inf <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_df, ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = dfbeta)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = c(-thr, thr), linetype = "dotted") +
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = label_df,
      ggplot2::aes(label = .id_val),
      vjust = -0.5,
      size  = 3
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title    = paste("Influence diagnostics for term:", term_name),
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Points labelled by ", id_var,
        " (top ", top_n_label, " |dfbeta|)."),
      x = x_lab,
      y = paste("dfbeta (change in log-hazard for", term_name, ")")
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
  
  outfile_inf <- file.path(dir_gl_influence, paste0("dfbeta_", term_name, ".png"))
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = outfile_inf,
    plot     = p_inf,
    width    = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300
  )
  
  message("Saved influence plot for term ", term_name, " to: ", outfile_inf)
}

# 5. CANDIDATE MODEL CREATION ####

violates_never_together <- function(vars, never_together) {
  any(vapply(
    never_together,
    function(bad_set) all(bad_set %in% vars),
    logical(1)
  ))
}

build_candidate_formulas <- function(
    fixed_main_covars,
    interaction_terms,
    required_interactions,
    must_have,
    never_together,
    max_main_effects,
    max_interactions,
    response_str,
    id_var,
    strata_covars = character(0)
) {
  ## Ensure these are plain character vectors
  interaction_terms    <- as.character(interaction_terms)
  required_interactions <- as.character(required_interactions)
  
  ## all subsets of main effects
  all_main_subsets <- unlist(
    lapply(seq_along(fixed_main_covars), function(k) {
      combn(fixed_main_covars, k, simplify = FALSE)
    }),
    recursive = FALSE
  )
  
  main_df <- tibble(main_terms = all_main_subsets) %>%
    mutate(
      n_main       = lengths(main_terms),
      has_must     = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ all(must_have %in% .x)),
      violates_bad = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ violates_never_together(.x, never_together))
    ) %>%
    filter(
      n_main <= max_main_effects,
      has_must,
      !violates_bad
    )
  
  ## For each main term set, add interactions that are consistent,
  ## enforcing required_interactions when their main effects are present
  add_interactions <- function(main_terms) {
    ## If there are no candidate interaction terms at all, just return "no interactions"
    if (length(interaction_terms) == 0L) {
      return(list(character(0)))
    }
    
    ## All interactions whose components are in main_terms
    allowed_int_all <- interaction_terms[
      vapply(
        strsplit(interaction_terms, ":", fixed = TRUE),
        function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
        logical(1)
      )
    ]
    
    ## Required interactions for this main term set
    if (length(required_interactions) > 0L) {
      required_int <- required_interactions[
        vapply(
          strsplit(required_interactions, ":", fixed = TRUE),
          function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
          logical(1)
        )
      ]
    } else {
      required_int <- character(0)
    }
    
    ## Optional interactions (allowed but not required)
    optional_int <- setdiff(allowed_int_all, required_int)
    
    ## If the number of required interactions exceeds max_interactions,
    ## this main-term set is not feasible (returns no interaction sets)
    if (length(required_int) > max_interactions) {
      return(list())
    }
    
    ## Always include at least the required interactions
    int_sets <- list(required_int)
    
    if (length(optional_int) == 0L || max_interactions <= length(required_int)) {
      ## No room or no optional interactions
      return(int_sets)
    }
    
    remaining_slots <- max_interactions - length(required_int)
    max_k <- min(remaining_slots, length(optional_int))
    
    for (k in 1:max_k) {
      opt_sets_k <- combn(optional_int, k, simplify = FALSE)
      ## each interaction set is required_int + some optional_int
      opt_sets_k <- lapply(opt_sets_k, function(x) c(required_int, x))
      int_sets   <- c(int_sets, opt_sets_k)
    }
    
    ## Remove possible duplicates of interaction sets
    int_sets_unique <- unique(lapply(int_sets, function(x) sort(as.character(x))))
    int_sets_unique
  }
  
  full_set <- main_df %>%
    mutate(
      interaction_sets = purrr::map(main_terms, add_interactions)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(interaction_sets) %>%
    mutate(
      all_terms     = purrr::map2(main_terms, interaction_sets, c),
      all_terms_chr = purrr::map_chr(all_terms, ~ paste(.x, collapse = " + "))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(all_terms_chr, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(all_terms_chr) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ## build strata() piece, if any
      strata_part = if (length(strata_covars) > 0L) {
        paste0(" + strata(", paste(strata_covars, collapse = ", "), ")")
      } else {
        ""
      },
      ## full coxph formula with frailty
      formula_coxph_chr  = paste0(
        response_str, " ~ ", all_terms_chr,
        strata_part,
        " + frailty(", id_var, ', distribution = "gaussian")'
      )
    )
  
  full_set %>%
    dplyr::select(
      all_terms_chr,  # keep for duplicate checking later
      main_terms,
      interaction_sets,
      all_terms,
      formula_coxph_chr
    )
}

## Build candidate models

)

# 6. FIT CANDIDATE MODELS (coxph + Gaussian frailty & parallel computing) ####

fit_one_coxph_frailty <- function(row, dat, dir_models) {
  model_id <- row$model_id
  f_coxph  <- as.formula(row$formula_coxph_chr)
  out_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    fit <- readRDS(out_file)
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      coxph(f_coxph, data = dat, ties = "efron"),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    saveRDS(fit, out_file)
  }
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = FALSE,
      logLik     = NA_real_,
      AIC        = NA_real_,
      nparams    = NA_integer_,
      message    = as.character(fit$message)
    )
  } else {
    LL     <- logLik(fit)
    ll_num <- as.numeric(LL)
    df     <- attr(LL, "df")
    aic    <- -2 * ll_num + 2 * df
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = TRUE,
      logLik     = ll_num,
      AIC        = aic,
      nparams    = df,
      message    = NA_character_
    )
  }
}

plan(multisession, workers = n_workers)

coxph_fit_summary <- candidate_models %>%
  split(.$batch_id) %>%
  purrr::imap_dfr(function(df_batch, b_id) {
    message("Fitting batch ", b_id, " (", nrow(df_batch), " models)")
    future_map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df_batch)), function(i) {
      fit_one_coxph_frailty(df_batch[i, ], dat = dat, dir_models = dir_models)
    })
  })

# 7. TEST PH ASSUMPTION (coxph + frailty(fish_id)) ####

ph_test_one_model <- function(model_id, dir_models, plot_dir, alpha = 0.05) {
  fit_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (!file.exists(fit_file)) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = "coxph frailty fit file not found"
    ))
  }
  
  fit <- readRDS(fit_file)
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = paste("coxph frailty fit is error object:", fit$message)
    ))
  }
  
  zph <- tryCatch(
    cox.zph(fit),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  
  if (inherits(zph, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = as.character(zph$message)
    ))
  }
  
  plot_file <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(model_id, "_schoenfeld.png"))
  png(plot_file, width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 150)
  par(mfrow = c(ceiling(nrow(zph$table) / 2), 2))
  plot(zph)
  dev.off()
  
  zph_tbl <- as.data.frame(zph$table)
  zph_tbl$term <- rownames(zph_tbl)
  
  zph_tbl <- zph_tbl %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::filter(term != "GLOBAL") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model_id = model_id, .before = 1)
  
  ph_ok <- !any(zph_tbl$p < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  list(
    model_id = model_id,
    ph_ok    = ph_ok,
    zph_tbl  = zph_tbl,
    error    = NA_character_
  )
}

ph_results_list <- future_map(
  candidate_models$model_id,
  ~ ph_test_one_model(.x, dir_models = dir_models, plot_dir = dir_ph_plots, alpha = alpha_ph)
)

ph_tables <- ph_results_list %>%
  purrr::keep(~ !is.null(.x$zph_tbl)) %>%

  dplyr::bind_rows()

)

)

# 11. MODEL AVERAGING ####
##  11.1: Build list ranked by AIC (MuMIn::model.sel), incl. null frailty model
##  11.2: Subset top models by ΔAIC threshold
##  11.3: Extract coefficients & HRs from top model (plus frailty variance)
##  11.4: Model-averaged coefficients (plus per-model frailty variance)

deltaAIC_threshold <- 2

coxph_fit_summary <- read.csv(out_file_summary)

valid_models <- coxph_fit_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(AIC) & is.finite(AIC))

model_ids <- valid_models$model_id

all_fits <- lapply(model_ids, function(mid) {
  readRDS(file.path(dir_models, paste0(mid, "_coxph.rds")))
})
names(all_fits) <- model_ids

## 11.1: null model: Surv(...) ~ frailty(fish_id)
null_formula <- as.formula(
  paste0(response_str, " ~ frailty(", id_var, ', distribution = "gaussian")')
)
null_fit <- coxph(null_formula, data = dat, ties = "efron")

null_model_id <- "M0_null"

all_fits_with_null <- c(
  setNames(list(null_fit), null_model_id),
  all_fits
)

models_all <- do.call(
  MuMIn::model.sel,
  c(all_fits_with_null, list(rank = "AIC"))
)

models_all_df <- as.data.frame(models_all)
models_all_df$model_id <- rownames(models_all_df)
models_all_df <- models_all_df %>%
  dplyr::select(model_id, dplyr::everything()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(AIC)

all_list_file <- file.path(outdir_root, "coxph_model_selection_all_MuMIn.csv")

write.csv(
  models_all_df,
  all_list_file,
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Full coxph+frailty model selection table (MuMIn, including null) saved to:\n",
    all_list_file, "\n")


## 11.2: Top candidate models (excluding null)
top_models <- subset(
  models_all,
  rownames(models_all) != null_model_id & delta <= deltaAIC_threshold
)

top_models_df <- as.data.frame(top_models)
top_models_df$model_id <- rownames(top_models_df)
top_models_df <- top_models_df %>%
  dplyr::select(model_id, dplyr::everything()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(AIC)

top_list_file <- file.path(
  outdir_root,
  paste0("coxph_model_selection_deltaAIC_", deltaAIC_threshold, "_MuMIn.csv")
)

write.csv(
  top_models_df,
  top_list_file,
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Top coxph+frailty models (ΔAIC <=", deltaAIC_threshold,
    ", excluding null) from MuMIn saved to:\n",
    top_list_file, "\n")


## Helper to extract frailty variance (theta) from coxph
get_frailty_var_coxph <- function(fit) {
  theta <- fit$history$`frailty(fish_id, distribution = "gaussian")`$theta
  if (is.null(theta) || length(theta) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(theta[1])
}

## 11.3: Top model coefficients + frailty variance
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; top-model coefficient table not created.")
} else {
  best_model_name <- rownames(top_models)[1]
  best_fit <- all_fits_with_null[[best_model_name]]
  
  beta <- coef(best_fit)
  vc   <- as.matrix(vcov(best_fit))
  se   <- sqrt(diag(vc))
  
  z_val <- beta / se
  p_val <- 2 * stats::pnorm(abs(z_val), lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  frail_var   <- get_frailty_var_coxph(best_fit)
  frail_sd    <- if (is.na(frail_var)) NA_real_ else sqrt(frail_var)
  
  top_model_coefs <- tibble::tibble(
    term         = names(beta),
    estimate     = as.numeric(beta),
    se           = as.numeric(se),
    z_value      = as.numeric(z_val),
    p_value      = as.numeric(p_val),
    HR           = as.numeric(HR),
    HR_lower_95  = as.numeric(HR_lower_95),
    HR_upper_95  = as.numeric(HR_upper_95),
    model_id     = best_model_name,
    frailty_var  = frail_var,
    frailty_sd   = frail_sd
  )
  
  out_file_top <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_top_model_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    top_model_coefs,
    out_file_top,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Top coxph+frailty model coefficients (with HR, 95% CI, and frailty variance) saved to:\n",
      out_file_top, "\n")
}


## 11.4: Model-averaged coefficients + per-model frailty variance
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; model averaging skipped.")
} else {
  avg_fit <- MuMIn::model.avg(top_models)
  avg_sum <- summary(avg_fit)
  
  avg_coefs <- as.data.frame(avg_sum$coefmat.full)
  avg_coefs$term <- rownames(avg_coefs)
  
  est_col <- "Estimate"
  se_col  <- if ("Std. Error" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "Std. Error"
  } else if ("SE" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "SE"
  } else {
    stop("Could not identify standard error column in avg_coefs.")
  }
  
  beta <- avg_coefs[[est_col]]
  se   <- avg_coefs[[se_col]]
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  avg_coefs$HR          <- HR
  avg_coefs$HR_lower_95 <- HR_lower_95
  avg_coefs$HR_upper_95 <- HR_upper_95
  
  avg_coefs <- avg_coefs %>%
    dplyr::select(
      term,
      dplyr::everything()
    )
  
  out_file_avg <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_model_averaged_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    avg_coefs,
    out_file_avg,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("MuMIn model-averaged coxph+frailty coefficients (with HR and 95% CI) saved to:\n",
      out_file_avg, "\n")
  
  ## Frailty variance for each top model
  top_model_names <- rownames(top_models)
  top_weights     <- top_models$weight
  
  frailty_info <- tibble::tibble(
    model_id = top_model_names,
    weight   = as.numeric(top_weights)
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      frailty_var = vapply(
        model_id,
        function(mid) get_frailty_var_coxph(all_fits_with_null[[mid]]),
        numeric(1)
      ),
      frailty_sd  = ifelse(is.na(frailty_var), NA_real_, sqrt(frailty_var))
    )
  
  out_file_frail <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_frailty_variance_top_models_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    frailty_info,
    out_file_frail,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Frailty variance for each top coxph model (with AIC weights) saved to:\n",
      out_file_frail, "\n")
}


# 12. SUBJECT-SPECIFIC CURVES ####

# Plot subject-specific curves for a hypothetical individual whose covariates are set at user-determined values

# This approach is analogous to predicting covariate effects for other regression models (GLM, GAM,...)
# We set values for the covariates of interest, and hold all other covariates static (often at their mean or median)
# This approach works well for showing the effect size implied by the model coefficients (model-based prediction) and for illustrating interactions, but their weakness is that they represent a hypothetical individual (not the population) and are sensitive to the chosen covariate values, meaning they can be misleading if the chosen covariate profile is unrealistic.

# 13. MARGINAL (ADJUSTED) CURVES ####

# Plot marginal (adjusted) curves that average predictions over the observed covariate distribution

# This approach provides estimates/predictions for a population in which everyone has the same focal value (e.g., diel period. = "night") but all other covariates are left at their original, observed values.
# This approach removes confounding, provides population-level effect of covariates, and is good for estimating causal effects, but can be more complex to explain, CIs require bootstrapping, and the magnitude of effects is smoothed by averaging.

# Description of this process (e.g., for manuscript):
# Instead of creating predictions from a hypothetical “average” fish with all covariates fixed at their mean values, 
# we used a g-computation approach that averages predictions across the actual distribution of all other covariates in the data set.
# In this framework, we intervene only on the covariates of interest (e.g., traps open or season), 
# while leaving every other covariate exactly as observed for each fish. 
# Predicted survival (or cumulative incidence) is generated for every individual under each counterfactual scenario, 
# and these predictions are then averaged to obtain population-level curves.
# This differs from the traditional “hold covariates at their mean” method, 
# which produces predictions for an artificial individual that may not exist and that does not reflect realistic combinations of covariates. 
# The g-computation approach yields curves that are fully adjusted, population-averaged, and interpretable at the ecological scale of interest.

library(riskRegression)
library(adjustedCurves)
library(rlang)

summary(best_fit)

# Prediction function

)

# Write a function that allows CIs to be plotted as steps
make_step_ribbon <- function(df) {
  # df must have columns: time, surv, lower, upper (plus grouping cols)
  df <- df[order(df$time), ]

  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(df)

  # start and end times for each step
  time_start <- df$time
  time_end   <- c(df$time[-1], df$time[nrow(df)])  # last step ends at last time

  # replicate each row twice
  out <- df[rep(seq_len(nrow(df)), each = 2), ]

  # assign stepped times: (t_i, t_{i+1}) for each original row
  out$time <- c(rbind(time_start, time_end))

  out
}

# Update CIs to be plotted as steps

  dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ make_step_ribbon(.x)) %>%
```

4. Rejection from the attempt zone (Z3) to the approach zone (Z2)

```{r rejection_cox_PH_frailty, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# This approach includes BOTH fence status and diel period main effects as covariates in the candidate models
# It also re-parameterizes smolt count such that it is only interpreted for levels of diel period where it varied during events (dawn, night, dusk);
# this is done instead of a diel X smolt interaction because smolt count is 0 for all rejection events during daytime periods
# Further, the reference level for fence status is set to "open" because smolt count needs to be interpreted during open periods, only

# We have also forced the inclusion of the fence_status main effect in every model, because fence operation effects are of primary interest

# If its inclusion is not forced, the top-ranked set of candidate models and model-averaged coefficients are analogous to the approach that only considers diel period

# A full explanation of model fitting decisions is in the manuscript.




# Option to fit mixed-effects Cox PH models w/ `coxph` function from `survival` package and w/ frailty term for random effect.

# Only works w/ one level for random effect (i.e., no nested random intercepts)

# 1. SETUP - USER-DEFINED OBJECTS ####

# Re-name the data set
rejection_frailty <- attempt_retreat

## Name of the data frame being used for analysis (for setting up analysis-specific directory)
data_name   <- "rejection_frailty"

## Name of the data set (for organizing outputs generated from different data)
dataset_name <- "rejection_frailty"

## Identify the data set being used for analysis
dat <- get(data_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)

# Check levels
table(dat$event, dat$twilight_period)
table(dat$event, dat$fence_status)

# Set diel reference levels for factors
levels(dat$twilight_period)
levels(dat$fence_status)
dat$twilight_period <- relevel(dat$twilight_period, ref = "night")
dat$fence_status <- relevel(dat$fence_status, ref = "open")

## Time-to-event variables
use_start_stop <- TRUE # TRUE if data set has time-varying covariates (tstart/tstop)
time_var   <- "tstop"   # "tstop" if using start-stop, otherwise "time"
tstart_var <- "tstart"  # only used if use_start_stop = TRUE
status_var <- "event"   # 0/1

## ID for random effect / clustering
id_var <- "fish_id"

## RE-PARAMETERIZE SMOLT COUNT SUCH THAT IT'S ONLY INTERPRETED FOR DAWN, DUSK, AND NIGHT
## BRIEF JUSTIFICATION AT TOP OF CODE CHUNK; FULL EXPLANATION IS IN THE MANUSCRIPT
## IT'S IMPORTANT THAT WE RE-PARAMETERIZE BEFORE STANDARDIZING
## “The continuous covariate was first re-parameterized to enforce structural constraints implied by the data and was subsequently standardized to facilitate model fitting and interpretation.”
dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(smolt_count_dark = if_else(twilight_period == "day", 0, smolt_count))
  
## Standardize continuous covariates that might appear in candidate models
dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    z.FL     = as.numeric(scale(FL_mm)),
    z.K      = as.numeric(scale(K)),
    z.season = as.numeric(scale(season)),
    z.smolts = as.numeric(scale(smolt_count_dark)) # NOTICE THAT WE'RE USING THE RE-PARAMETERIZED VERSION OF SMOLT COUNT
  )

## Covariates that might appear in models (fixed effects)
fixed_main_covars <- c(
  "z.FL",
  "z.K",
  "z.season",
  "twilight_period",
  "fence_status",
  "z.smolts"
)

## Which of those covariates are continuous?
continuous_covars <- c("z.FL", "z.K", "z.season", "z.smolts")

## Continuous covariates (on original scale) that are used for testing the assumption of linearity and to identify extreme outliers
linearity_raw_covars <- c("FL_mm", "K", "season", "smolt_count")

## (Optional) covariates that must always be present in any candidate model
must_have <- c("fence_status") 
#must_have <- character(0)

## (Optional) interactions that may be included in candidate models
## (must be specified as "var1:var2" using names from fixed_main_covariates)
# interaction_terms <- c("twilight_period:fence_status",
#                        "twilight_period:z.season",
#                        "z.smolts:z.season")

interaction_terms <- c("twilight_period:z.season",
                       "z.smolts:z.season")
# interaction_terms <- character(0) # Use this if interaction terms are not included

## (Optional) interactions that MUST be included whenever their main effects are present
## Must be a subset of interaction_terms.
#required_interactions <- c("twilight_period:fence_status")
required_interactions <- character(0) # e.g., c("twilight_period:z.season")

if (!all(required_interactions %in% interaction_terms)) {
  stop("All required_interactions must also appear in interaction_terms.")
}

## (Optional) covariates that must be used for stratification in every model
# Make sure strata variables are NOT in fixed_main_covars
#strata_covars <- "fence_status"
strata_covars <- character(0)

## (Optional) illegal combinations: lists of covariates that cannot appear in the same model
#never_together <- list(c("z.FL", "z.K")) # High colinearity
never_together <- list() # Use this if illegal combinations do not need to be specified

## Determine the max parameters per model
## Target events-per-variable (EPV) rule (per fixed effect, not counting frailty)
target_epv <- 10L

## Count the number of events in the data
if (!status_var %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("status_var ('", status_var, "') not found in dat.")
}
n_events <- sum(dat[[status_var]] == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)

## Max number of fixed-effect "slots" (main effects + interactions)
max_effects_total <- max(1L, floor(n_events / target_epv))

if (max_effects_total < 3L) {
  warning(
    "Relatively few events (n_events = ", n_events, 
    "); max_effects_total = ", max_effects_total,
    ". Consider simplifying the candidate model set."
  )
}

## Basic counts of what is available
n_main_available <- length(fixed_main_covars)
n_int_available  <- length(interaction_terms)
n_must           <- length(must_have)

if (n_must > 0L && !all(must_have %in% fixed_main_covars)) {
  stop("All 'must_have' covariates must appear in fixed_main_covars.")
}

## Ensure we can at least include all must-have main effects
if (n_must > max_effects_total) {
  warning(
    "Number of must_have covariates (", n_must, 
    ") exceeds EPV-based max_effects_total (", max_effects_total, ").\n",
    "Forcing max_effects_total = n_must so all must_have terms can be included, ",
    "but this may overfit given the number of events."
  )
  max_effects_total <- n_must
}

## Budget left after forcing must_have main effects
remaining_budget <- max(0L, max_effects_total - n_must)

## Allocate at most half of the non-must budget to interactions
max_interactions <- 0L
if (n_int_available > 0L && remaining_budget > 0L) {
  max_interactions <- min(
    n_int_available,
    floor(remaining_budget / 2L)
  )
}

## Remaining slots go to *additional* main effects beyond must_have
additional_mains <- remaining_budget - max_interactions
max_main_effects <- n_must + min(
  additional_mains,
  max(0L, n_main_available - n_must)
)

message(
  "Events: ", n_events,
  " | target EPV (per fixed effect): ", target_epv,
  " | max_effects_total (main + interaction) = ", max_effects_total,
  "\n  max_main_effects = ", max_main_effects,
  " (including ", n_must, " must_have terms)",
  "\n  max_interactions = ", max_interactions,
  " (frailty(", id_var, ") handled separately)."
)

## Manually set max fixed effects and max number of interactions
## Max number of main effects allowed in any model (excluding interactions)
max_main_effects <- 6

## Maximum number of interactions allowed in any model
max_interactions <- 3

## Parallel computing settings
n_workers <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1)
future_globals_maxSize_GB <- 4  # memory ceiling for future (in GB)

## Significance level for PH violations
alpha_ph <- 0.05

## Build Surv() expression as a string
if (!use_start_stop) {
  response_str <- sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var)
} else {
  response_str <- sprintf("Surv(%s, %s, %s)", tstart_var, time_var, status_var)
}

response_formula <- as.formula(paste(response_str, "~ 1"))

## Collapse intervals where covariate values do not change
## And, remove columns not needed for modeling

core_vars <- c(
  id_var,
  status_var,
  time_var,
  if (use_start_stop) tstart_var,
  "interval_id"
)

extra_keep_vars <- c(
  linearity_raw_covars,
  "tstart_datetime",
  "tstop_datetime"
)

keep_vars <- unique(c(core_vars, model_covars, extra_keep_vars))

dat <- dat[, intersect(keep_vars, names(dat))]

if (!"interval_id" %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("interval_id column is required for collapsing but is not present in dat.")
}

collapse_covars <- intersect(model_covars, names(dat))

if ("tstart_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstart_datetime"
} else if ("tstop_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstop_datetime"
} else {
  order_var <- if (use_start_stop) tstart_var else time_var
}

dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data[[order_var]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    across(
      all_of(collapse_covars),
      ~ . != dplyr::lag(.),
      .names = "chg_{.col}"
    ),
    any_cov_change = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1L,
      TRUE,
      {
        chg_mat <- dplyr::across(
          dplyr::starts_with("chg_"),
          ~ ifelse(is.na(.), FALSE, .)
        )
        if (ncol(chg_mat) == 0L) {
          FALSE
        } else {
          rowSums(chg_mat) > 0
        }
      }
    ),
    event_here = .data[[status_var]] == 1L,
    boundary   = any_cov_change | event_here,
    collapse_id = cumsum(boundary)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::starts_with("chg_")) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id, collapse_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    !!sym(tstart_var) := min(.data[[tstart_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(time_var)   := max(.data[[time_var]],   na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(status_var) := max(.data[[status_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = -dplyr::any_of(c("interval_id", "collapse_id",
                               tstart_var, time_var, status_var)),
      .fns  = ~ dplyr::first(.)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(collapse_id, any_cov_change, event_here, boundary)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_id, .data[[tstart_var]])

message("After collapsing within interval_id: ", nrow(dat),

# 5. CANDIDATE MODEL CREATION ####

violates_never_together <- function(vars, never_together) {
  any(vapply(
    never_together,
    function(bad_set) all(bad_set %in% vars),
    logical(1)
  ))
}

build_candidate_formulas <- function(
    fixed_main_covars,
    interaction_terms,
    required_interactions,
    must_have,
    never_together,
    max_main_effects,
    max_interactions,
    response_str,
    id_var,
    strata_covars = character(0)
) {
  ## Ensure these are plain character vectors
  interaction_terms    <- as.character(interaction_terms)
  required_interactions <- as.character(required_interactions)
  
  ## all subsets of main effects
  all_main_subsets <- unlist(
    lapply(seq_along(fixed_main_covars), function(k) {
      combn(fixed_main_covars, k, simplify = FALSE)
    }),
    recursive = FALSE
  )
  
  main_df <- tibble(main_terms = all_main_subsets) %>%
    mutate(
      n_main       = lengths(main_terms),
      has_must     = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ all(must_have %in% .x)),
      violates_bad = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ violates_never_together(.x, never_together))
    ) %>%
    filter(
      n_main <= max_main_effects,
      has_must,
      !violates_bad
    )
  
  ## For each main term set, add interactions that are consistent,
  ## enforcing required_interactions when their main effects are present
  add_interactions <- function(main_terms) {
    ## If there are no candidate interaction terms at all, just return "no interactions"
    if (length(interaction_terms) == 0L) {
      return(list(character(0)))
    }
    
    ## All interactions whose components are in main_terms
    allowed_int_all <- interaction_terms[
      vapply(
        strsplit(interaction_terms, ":", fixed = TRUE),
        function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
        logical(1)
      )
    ]
    
    ## Required interactions for this main term set
    if (length(required_interactions) > 0L) {
      required_int <- required_interactions[
        vapply(
          strsplit(required_interactions, ":", fixed = TRUE),
          function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
          logical(1)
        )
      ]
    } else {
      required_int <- character(0)
    }
    
    ## Optional interactions (allowed but not required)
    optional_int <- setdiff(allowed_int_all, required_int)
    
    ## If the number of required interactions exceeds max_interactions,
    ## this main-term set is not feasible (returns no interaction sets)
    if (length(required_int) > max_interactions) {
      return(list())
    }
    
    ## Always include at least the required interactions
    int_sets <- list(required_int)
    
    if (length(optional_int) == 0L || max_interactions <= length(required_int)) {
      ## No room or no optional interactions
      return(int_sets)
    }
    
    remaining_slots <- max_interactions - length(required_int)
    max_k <- min(remaining_slots, length(optional_int))
    
    for (k in 1:max_k) {
      opt_sets_k <- combn(optional_int, k, simplify = FALSE)
      ## each interaction set is required_int + some optional_int
      opt_sets_k <- lapply(opt_sets_k, function(x) c(required_int, x))
      int_sets   <- c(int_sets, opt_sets_k)
    }
    
    ## Remove possible duplicates of interaction sets
    int_sets_unique <- unique(lapply(int_sets, function(x) sort(as.character(x))))
    int_sets_unique
  }
  
  full_set <- main_df %>%
    mutate(
      interaction_sets = purrr::map(main_terms, add_interactions)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::unnest(interaction_sets) %>%
    mutate(
      all_terms     = purrr::map2(main_terms, interaction_sets, c),
      all_terms_chr = purrr::map_chr(all_terms, ~ paste(.x, collapse = " + "))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(all_terms_chr, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(all_terms_chr) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ## build strata() piece, if any
      strata_part = if (length(strata_covars) > 0L) {
        paste0(" + strata(", paste(strata_covars, collapse = ", "), ")")
      } else {
        ""
      },
      ## full coxph formula with frailty
      formula_coxph_chr  = paste0(
        response_str, " ~ ", all_terms_chr,
        strata_part,
        " + frailty(", id_var, ', distribution = "gaussian")'
      )
    )
  
  full_set %>%
    dplyr::select(
      all_terms_chr,  # keep for duplicate checking later
      main_terms,
      interaction_sets,
      all_terms,
      formula_coxph_chr
    )
}

## Build candidate models
candidate_models <- build_candidate_formulas(
  fixed_main_covars     = fixed_main_covars,
  interaction_terms     = interaction_terms,
  required_interactions = required_interactions,
  must_have             = must_have,
  never_together        = never_together,
  max_main_effects      = max_main_effects,
  max_interactions      = max_interactions,
  response_str          = response_str,
  id_var                = id_var,
  strata_covars         = strata_covars
)

## Remove any duplicate formulas and reassign model IDs
n_before <- nrow(candidate_models)
candidate_models <- candidate_models %>%
  dplyr::distinct(formula_coxph_chr, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(model_id = paste0("M", dplyr::row_number())) %>%
  dplyr::relocate(model_id, .before = 1)

n_after <- nrow(candidate_models)
if (n_after < n_before) {

}

# 6. FIT CANDIDATE MODELS (coxph + Gaussian frailty & parallel computing) ####

batch_size <- 10   

candidate_models <- candidate_models %>%
  dplyr::mutate(batch_id = ceiling(dplyr::row_number() / batch_size))

fit_one_coxph_frailty <- function(row, dat, dir_models) {
  model_id <- row$model_id
  f_coxph  <- as.formula(row$formula_coxph_chr)
  out_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    fit <- readRDS(out_file)
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      coxph(f_coxph, data = dat, ties = "efron"),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    saveRDS(fit, out_file)
  }
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = FALSE,
      logLik     = NA_real_,
      AIC        = NA_real_,
      nparams    = NA_integer_,
      message    = as.character(fit$message)
    )
  } else {
    LL     <- logLik(fit)
    ll_num <- as.numeric(LL)
    df     <- attr(LL, "df")
    aic    <- -2 * ll_num + 2 * df
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = TRUE,
      logLik     = ll_num,
      AIC        = aic,
      nparams    = df,
      message    = NA_character_
    )
  }
}

plan(multisession, workers = n_workers)

coxph_fit_summary <- candidate_models %>%
  split(.$batch_id) %>%
  purrr::imap_dfr(function(df_batch, b_id) {
    message("Fitting batch ", b_id, " (", nrow(df_batch), " models)")
    future_map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df_batch)), function(i) {
      fit_one_coxph_frailty(df_batch[i, ], dat = dat, dir_models = dir_models)
    })
  })

# 7. TEST PH ASSUMPTION (coxph + frailty(fish_id)) ####

ph_test_one_model <- function(model_id, dir_models, plot_dir, alpha = 0.05) {
  fit_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (!file.exists(fit_file)) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = "coxph frailty fit file not found"
    ))
  }
  
  fit <- readRDS(fit_file)
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = paste("coxph frailty fit is error object:", fit$message)
    ))
  }
  
  zph <- tryCatch(
    cox.zph(fit),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  
  if (inherits(zph, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = as.character(zph$message)
    ))
  }
  
  plot_file <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(model_id, "_schoenfeld.png"))
  png(plot_file, width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 150)
  par(mfrow = c(ceiling(nrow(zph$table) / 2), 2))
  plot(zph)
  dev.off()
  
  zph_tbl <- as.data.frame(zph$table)
  zph_tbl$term <- rownames(zph_tbl)
  
  zph_tbl <- zph_tbl %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::filter(term != "GLOBAL") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model_id = model_id, .before = 1)
  
  ph_ok <- !any(zph_tbl$p < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  list(
    model_id = model_id,
    ph_ok    = ph_ok,
    zph_tbl  = zph_tbl,
    error    = NA_character_
  )
}

ph_results_list <- future_map(

batch_size <- 10

  dplyr::mutate(batch_id = ceiling(dplyr::row_number() / batch_size))

fit_one_coxph_frailty <- function(row, dat, dir_models) {
  model_id <- row$model_id
  f_coxph  <- as.formula(row$formula_coxph_chr)
  out_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    fit <- readRDS(out_file)
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      coxph(f_coxph, data = dat, ties = "efron"),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    saveRDS(fit, out_file)
  }
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      formula    = row$formula_coxph_chr,
      logLik     = NA_real_,
      AIC        = NA_real_,
      deltaAIC   = NA_real_,
      weight     = NA_real_,
      nparams    = NA_integer_,
      message    = as.character(fit$message)
    )
  } else {
    LL     <- logLik(fit)
    ll_num <- as.numeric(LL)
    df     <- attr(LL, "df")
    aic    <- -2 * ll_num + 2 * df
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      formula    = row$formula_coxph_chr,
      logLik     = ll_num,
      AIC        = aic,
      deltaAIC   = NA_real_,
      weight     = NA_real_,
      nparams    = df,
      message    = NA_character_
    )
  }
}

plan(multisession, workers = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))

  purrr::imap_dfr(function(df_batch, b_id) {
    message("Refitting batch ", b_id, " (", nrow(df_batch), " models)")
    future_map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df_batch)), function(i) {
      fit_one_coxph_frailty(df_batch[i, ], dat = dat, dir_models = dir_models)
    })
  })

##  11.1: Build list ranked by AIC (MuMIn::model.sel), incl. null frailty model
##  11.2: Subset top models by ΔAIC threshold
##  11.3: Extract coefficients & HRs from top model (plus frailty variance)
```
