```{r rejection_cox_PH_frailty, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
## Helper to extract frailty variance (theta) from coxph
get_frailty_var_coxph <- function(fit) {
  theta <- fit$history$`frailty(fish_id, distribution = "gaussian")`$theta
  if (is.null(theta) || length(theta) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(theta[1])
}

## 11.3: Top model coefficients + frailty variance
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; top-model coefficient table not created.")
} else {
  best_model_name <- rownames(top_models)[1]
  best_fit <- all_fits_with_null[[best_model_name]]
  
  beta <- coef(best_fit)
  vc   <- as.matrix(vcov(best_fit))
  se   <- sqrt(diag(vc))
  
  z_val <- beta / se
  p_val <- 2 * stats::pnorm(abs(z_val), lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  frail_var   <- get_frailty_var_coxph(best_fit)
  frail_sd    <- if (is.na(frail_var)) NA_real_ else sqrt(frail_var)
  
  top_model_coefs <- tibble::tibble(
    term         = names(beta),
    estimate     = as.numeric(beta),
    se           = as.numeric(se),
    z_value      = as.numeric(z_val),
    p_value      = as.numeric(p_val),
    HR           = as.numeric(HR),
    HR_lower_95  = as.numeric(HR_lower_95),
    HR_upper_95  = as.numeric(HR_upper_95),
    model_id     = best_model_name,
    frailty_var  = frail_var,
    frailty_sd   = frail_sd
  )
  
  out_file_top <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_top_model_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    top_model_coefs,
    out_file_top,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Top coxph+frailty model coefficients (with HR, 95% CI, and frailty variance) saved to:\n",
      out_file_top, "\n")
}


## 11.4: Model-averaged coefficients + per-model frailty variance
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; model averaging skipped.")
} else {
  avg_fit <- MuMIn::model.avg(top_models)
  avg_sum <- summary(avg_fit)
  
  avg_coefs <- as.data.frame(avg_sum$coefmat.full)
  avg_coefs$term <- rownames(avg_coefs)
  
  est_col <- "Estimate"
  se_col  <- if ("Std. Error" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "Std. Error"
  } else if ("SE" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "SE"
  } else {
    stop("Could not identify standard error column in avg_coefs.")
  }
  
  beta <- avg_coefs[[est_col]]
  se   <- avg_coefs[[se_col]]
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  avg_coefs$HR          <- HR
  avg_coefs$HR_lower_95 <- HR_lower_95
  avg_coefs$HR_upper_95 <- HR_upper_95
  
  avg_coefs <- avg_coefs %>%
    dplyr::select(
      term,
      dplyr::everything()
    )
  
  out_file_avg <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_model_averaged_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    avg_coefs,
    out_file_avg,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("MuMIn model-averaged coxph+frailty coefficients (with HR and 95% CI) saved to:\n",
      out_file_avg, "\n")
  
  ## Frailty variance for each top model
  top_model_names <- rownames(top_models)
  top_weights     <- top_models$weight
  
  frailty_info <- tibble::tibble(
    model_id = top_model_names,
    weight   = as.numeric(top_weights)
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      frailty_var = vapply(
        model_id,
        function(mid) get_frailty_var_coxph(all_fits_with_null[[mid]]),
        numeric(1)
      ),
      frailty_sd  = ifelse(is.na(frailty_var), NA_real_, sqrt(frailty_var))
    )
  
  out_file_frail <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_frailty_variance_top_models_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    frailty_info,
    out_file_frail,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Frailty variance for each top coxph model (with AIC weights) saved to:\n",
      out_file_frail, "\n")
}

# 13. MARGINAL (ADJUSTED) CURVES ####

# Plot marginal (adjusted) curves that average predictions over the observed covariate distribution

# This approach provides estimates/predictions for a population in which everyone has the same focal value (e.g., diel period. = "night") but all other covariates are left at their original, observed values.
# This approach removes confounding, provides population-level effect of covariates, and is good for estimating causal effects, but can be more complex to explain, CIs require bootstrapping, and the magnitude of effects is smoothed by averaging.

# Description of this process (e.g., for manuscript):
# Instead of creating predictions from a hypothetical “average” fish with all covariates fixed at their mean values, 
# we used a g-computation approach that averages predictions across the actual distribution of all other covariates in the data set.
# In this framework, we intervene only on the covariates of interest (e.g., traps open or season), 
# while leaving every other covariate exactly as observed for each fish. 
# Predicted survival (or cumulative incidence) is generated for every individual under each counterfactual scenario, 
# and these predictions are then averaged to obtain population-level curves.
# This differs from the traditional “hold covariates at their mean” method, 
# which produces predictions for an artificial individual that may not exist and that does not reflect realistic combinations of covariates. 
# The g-computation approach yields curves that are fully adjusted, population-averaged, and interpretable at the ecological scale of interest.

library(riskRegression)
library(adjustedCurves)
library(rlang)

summary(best_fit)

m1 <- coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ z.FL + z.season * twilight_period + fence_status + frailty(fish_id, distribution = "gamma"), data = dat, 
            x = TRUE, y = TRUE, ties = "efron")

table(dat$event, dat$twilight_period)
levels(dat$twilight_period)

summary(m1)

# Prediction function
pred_surv <- function(...) {
  1 - predictRisk(...)
}

# Plot predicted effect of diel period w/out the seasonal effect set manually
# To include CIs, we need to plot bootstrapped estimates

adjsurv <- adjustedsurv(
  data          = dat,
  variable      = "twilight_period",  # factor or binary covariate
  ev_time       = "tstop",
  event         = "event",
  method        = "direct",   # standard g-computation
  outcome_model = m1,
  predict_fun   = pred_surv,
  conf_int = TRUE,
  bootstrap = TRUE,
  n_boot = 200
)

# Write a function that allows CIs to be plotted as steps
make_step_ribbon <- function(df) {
  # df must have columns: time, surv, lower, upper (plus grouping cols)
  df <- df[order(df$time), ]

  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(df)

  # start and end times for each step
  time_start <- df$time
  time_end   <- c(df$time[-1], df$time[nrow(df)])  # last step ends at last time

  # replicate each row twice
  out <- df[rep(seq_len(nrow(df)), each = 2), ]

  # assign stepped times: (t_i, t_{i+1}) for each original row
  out$time <- c(rbind(time_start, time_end))

  out
}

  dplyr::group_modify(~ make_step_ribbon(.x)) %>%

b <- coef(m1)
V <- vcov(m1)

se_hat   <- sqrt( t(L) %*% V[names(L), names(L)] %*% L )

HR  <- exp(beta_hat)
CI  <- exp(beta_hat + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_hat)
```

5. Passage

The effect of traps open can only be interpreted for dusk and night periods since no contrasts were observed for day and dawn.

Similarly, although diel period is included in the model and no effect is detected, events predominantly occurred at night.

```{r passage_cox_PH_traps_open, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# Fit w/ coxph(); not a mixed effects model because passage is a terminal event (each smolt can only pass once).

# 1. SETUP - USER-DEFINED OBJECTS ####

# Re-name the data set
passage_traps_open <- attempt_advance

## Name of the data frame being used for analysis (for setting up analysis-specific directory)
data_name   <- "passage_traps_open"

## Name of the data set (for organizing outputs generated from different data)
dataset_name <- "passage_traps_open"

## Identify the data set being used for analysis
dat <- get(data_name, envir = .GlobalEnv)

# Check factor levels
levels(dat$traps_open)
dat$traps_open <- relevel(dat$traps_open, ref = "one")

## Time-to-event variables
use_start_stop <- TRUE # TRUE if data set has time-varying covariates (tstart/tstop)
time_var   <- "tstop"   # "tstop" if using start-stop, otherwise "time"
tstart_var <- "tstart"  # only used if use_start_stop = TRUE
status_var <- "event"   # 0/1

## Standardize continuous covariates that might appear in candidate models
dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    z.FL     = as.numeric(scale(FL_mm)),
    z.K      = as.numeric(scale(K)),
    z.season = as.numeric(scale(season)),
    z.smolts = as.numeric(scale(smolt_count))
  )

## Covariates that might appear in models (fixed effects)
## IMPORTANT: Do not include here any variables you want to appear only as strata().
fixed_main_covars <- c(
  "z.FL",
  "z.K",
  "z.season",
  "traps_open",
  "z.smolts"
)

## Which of those covariates are continuous?
continuous_covars <- c("z.FL", "z.K", "z.season", "z.smolts")

## Continuous covariates (on original scale) that are used for testing linearity / outliers
linearity_raw_covars <- c("FL_mm", "K", "season", "smolt_count")

## (Optional) covariates that must always be present in any candidate model
must_have <- c("traps_open") 
#must_have <- character(0)

## (Optional) interactions that may be included in candidate models
## (must be specified as "var1:var2" using names from fixed_main_covars)
interaction_terms <- c("z.smolts:z.season",
                       "z.smolts:traps_open")
# interaction_terms <- character(0)

## (Optional) interactions that MUST be included whenever their main effects are present
## e.g., if a model contains both z.smolts and traps_open, it MUST include z.smolts:traps_open
forced_interactions <- character(0)
# forced_interactions <- c("z.smolts:traps_open")

## (Optional) illegal combinations: lists of covariates that cannot appear in the same model
#never_together <- list(c("z.FL", "z.K"))
never_together <- list()

## (Optional) covariates that must be stratified in each model via strata()
## These should NOT also appear in fixed_main_covars.
strat_vars <- c("fence_status")
#strat_vars <- character(0)

## Determine the max parameters per model
## Target events-per-variable (EPV) rule (per fixed effect)
target_epv <- 10L

## Count the number of events in the data
if (!status_var %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("status_var ('", status_var, "') not found in dat.")
}
n_events <- sum(dat[[status_var]] == 1L, na.rm = TRUE)

## Max number of fixed-effect "slots" (main effects + interactions)
max_effects_total <- max(1L, floor(n_events / target_epv))

if (max_effects_total < 3L) {
  warning(
    "Relatively few events (n_events = ", n_events, 
    "); max_effects_total = ", max_effects_total,
    ". Consider simplifying the candidate model set."
  )
}

## Basic counts of what is available
n_main_available <- length(fixed_main_covars)
n_int_available  <- length(interaction_terms)
n_must           <- length(must_have)

if (n_must > 0L && !all(must_have %in% fixed_main_covars)) {
  stop("All 'must_have' covariates must appear in fixed_main_covars.")
}

## Ensure we can at least include all must-have main effects
if (n_must > max_effects_total) {
  warning(
    "Number of must_have covariates (", n_must, 
    ") exceeds EPV-based max_effects_total (", max_effects_total, ").\n",
    "Forcing max_effects_total = n_must so all must_have terms can be included, ",
    "but this may overfit given the number of events."
  )
  max_effects_total <- n_must
}

## Budget left after forcing must_have main effects
remaining_budget <- max(0L, max_effects_total - n_must)

## Allocate at most half of the non-must budget to interactions
max_interactions <- 0L
if (n_int_available > 0L && remaining_budget > 0L) {
  max_interactions <- min(
    n_int_available,
    floor(remaining_budget / 2L)
  )
}

## Remaining slots go to *additional* main effects beyond must_have
additional_mains <- remaining_budget - max_interactions
max_main_effects <- n_must + min(
  additional_mains,
  max(0L, n_main_available - n_must)
)

message(
  "Events: ", n_events,
  " | target EPV (per fixed effect): ", target_epv,
  " | max_effects_total (main + interaction) = ", max_effects_total,
  "\n  max_main_effects = ", max_main_effects,
  " (including ", n_must, " must_have terms)",
  "\n  max_interactions = ", max_interactions, "."
)

## Manually set max fixed effects and max number of interactions (override EPV if desired)

} else {

}

## Collapse intervals where covariate values do not change
## And, remove columns not needed for modeling

core_vars <- c(
  status_var,
  time_var,
  if (use_start_stop) tstart_var,
  "interval_id"
)

## Model covariates: fixed effects + stratification variables
model_covars <- unique(c(fixed_main_covars, strat_vars))

extra_keep_vars <- c(
  linearity_raw_covars,
  "tstart_datetime",
  "tstop_datetime"
)

keep_vars <- unique(c(core_vars, model_covars, extra_keep_vars))

dat <- dat[, intersect(keep_vars, names(dat))]

if (!"interval_id" %in% names(dat)) {
  stop("interval_id column is required for collapsing but is not present in dat.")
}

collapse_covars <- intersect(model_covars, names(dat))

if ("tstart_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstart_datetime"
} else if ("tstop_datetime" %in% names(dat)) {
  order_var <- "tstop_datetime"
} else {
  order_var <- if (use_start_stop) tstart_var else time_var
}

dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data[[order_var]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    across(
      all_of(collapse_covars),
      ~ . != dplyr::lag(.),
      .names = "chg_{.col}"
    ),
    any_cov_change = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1L,
      TRUE,
      {
        chg_mat <- dplyr::across(
          dplyr::starts_with("chg_"),
          ~ ifelse(is.na(.), FALSE, .)
        )
        if (ncol(chg_mat) == 0L) {
          FALSE
        } else {
          rowSums(chg_mat) > 0
        }
      }
    ),
    event_here  = .data[[status_var]] == 1L,
    boundary    = any_cov_change | event_here,
    collapse_id = cumsum(boundary)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::starts_with("chg_")) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(interval_id, collapse_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    !!sym(tstart_var) := min(.data[[tstart_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(time_var)   := max(.data[[time_var]],   na.rm = TRUE),
    !!sym(status_var) := max(.data[[status_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
    dplyr::across(
      .cols = -dplyr::any_of(c("interval_id", "collapse_id",
                               tstart_var, time_var, status_var)),
      .fns  = ~ dplyr::first(.)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(collapse_id, any_cov_change, event_here, boundary)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(interval_id, .data[[tstart_var]])

message("After collapsing within interval_id: ", nrow(dat),

# 5. CANDIDATE MODEL CREATION ####

violates_never_together <- function(vars, never_together) {
  any(vapply(
    never_together,
    function(bad_set) all(bad_set %in% vars),
    logical(1)
  ))
}

build_candidate_formulas <- function(
    fixed_main_covars,
    interaction_terms,
    must_have,
    never_together,
    max_main_effects,
    max_interactions,
    response_str,
    strat_vars,
    forced_interactions = character(0)
) {
  ## Ensure forced_interactions is a subset of interaction_terms
  forced_interactions <- intersect(forced_interactions, interaction_terms)
  
  ## all subsets of main effects
  all_main_subsets <- unlist(
    lapply(seq_along(fixed_main_covars), function(k) {
      combn(fixed_main_covars, k, simplify = FALSE)
    }),
    recursive = FALSE
  )
  
  main_df <- tibble(main_terms = all_main_subsets) %>%
    mutate(
      n_main       = lengths(main_terms),
      has_must     = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ all(must_have %in% .x)),
      violates_bad = purrr::map_lgl(main_terms, ~ violates_never_together(.x, never_together))
    ) %>%
    filter(
      n_main <= max_main_effects,
      has_must,
      !violates_bad
    )
  
  ## For each main-term set, build allowed interaction sets,
  ## enforcing forced_interactions whenever their main effects are present.
  add_interactions <- function(main_terms) {
    ## Interactions whose BOTH main effects are in main_terms
    allowed_int <- interaction_terms[
      vapply(
        strsplit(interaction_terms, ":", fixed = TRUE),
        function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
        logical(1)
      )
    ]
    
    ## Forced interactions whose main effects are present
    forced_here <- forced_interactions[
      vapply(
        strsplit(forced_interactions, ":", fixed = TRUE),
        function(xx) all(xx %in% main_terms),
        logical(1)
      )
    ]
    
    ## If we would exceed the interaction budget just with forced terms,
    ## this main_terms set is infeasible under the EPV constraints.
    if (length(forced_here) > max_interactions) {
      return(list())  # no valid interaction sets for this main_terms
    }
    
    ## Optional interactions are allowed_int minus the ones we’re forcing
    optional_int <- setdiff(allowed_int, forced_here)
    
    int_sets <- list()
    
    if (length(forced_here) == 0L) {
      ## If nothing is forced, we allow "no interactions" as a valid option
      int_sets <- list(character(0))
    } else {
      ## At minimum, the interaction set must contain all forced_here
      int_sets <- list(forced_here)
    }
    
    ## How many extra optional interactions can we add beyond forced_here?
    max_extra <- max(0L, max_interactions - length(forced_here))
    
    if (max_extra > 0L && length(optional_int) > 0L) {
      max_k <- min(max_extra, length(optional_int))
      for (k in 1:max_k) {
        opt_sets_k <- combn(optional_int, k, simplify = FALSE)
        for (s in opt_sets_k) {
          int_sets <- c(int_sets, list(c(forced_here, s)))
        }
      }
    }
    
    int_sets
  }
  
  ## strata() part
  strata_part <- if (length(strat_vars) > 0) {
    paste0(" + strata(", paste(strat_vars, collapse = ", "), ")")
  } else {
    ""
  }
  
  full_set <- main_df %>%
    mutate(
      interaction_sets = purrr::map(main_terms, add_interactions)
    ) %>%
    ## drop main-term sets with no feasible interaction sets
    tidyr::unnest(interaction_sets) %>%
    mutate(
      all_terms     = purrr::map2(main_terms, interaction_sets, c),
      all_terms_chr = purrr::map_chr(all_terms, ~ paste(.x, collapse = " + "))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(all_terms_chr, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(all_terms_chr) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      model_id          = paste0("M", dplyr::row_number()),
      formula_coxph_chr = paste0(
        response_str, " ~ ", all_terms_chr,
        strata_part
      )
    )
  
  full_set %>%
    dplyr::select(model_id, main_terms, interaction_sets, all_terms, formula_coxph_chr)
}


candidate_models <- build_candidate_formulas(
  fixed_main_covars = fixed_main_covars,
  interaction_terms = interaction_terms,
  must_have         = must_have,

  max_main_effects  = max_main_effects,
  max_interactions  = max_interactions,
  response_str      = response_str,
  strat_vars        = strat_vars,
  forced_interactions = forced_interactions
)

batch_size <- 10

  dplyr::mutate(batch_id = ceiling(dplyr::row_number() / batch_size))

fit_one_coxph <- function(row, dat, dir_models) {
  model_id <- row$model_id
  f_coxph  <- as.formula(row$formula_coxph_chr)
  out_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (file.exists(out_file)) {
    fit <- readRDS(out_file)
  } else {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      coxph(f_coxph, data = dat, ties = "efron"),
      error = function(e) e
    )
    saveRDS(fit, out_file)
  }
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = FALSE,
      logLik     = NA_real_,
      AIC        = NA_real_,
      nparams    = NA_integer_,
      message    = as.character(fit$message)
    )
  } else {
    LL     <- logLik(fit)
    ll_num <- as.numeric(LL)
    df     <- attr(LL, "df")
    aic    <- -2 * ll_num + 2 * df
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      converged  = TRUE,
      logLik     = ll_num,
      AIC        = aic,
      nparams    = df,
      message    = NA_character_
    )
  }
}

plan(multisession, workers = n_workers)

  purrr::imap_dfr(function(df_batch, b_id) {
    message("Fitting batch ", b_id, " (", nrow(df_batch), " models)")
    future_map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df_batch)), function(i) {
      fit_one_coxph(df_batch[i, ], dat = dat, dir_models = dir_models)
    })
  })

# 7. TEST PH ASSUMPTION (plain coxph models) ####

ph_test_one_model <- function(model_id, dir_models, plot_dir, alpha = 0.05) {
  fit_file <- file.path(dir_models, paste0(model_id, "_coxph.rds"))
  
  if (!file.exists(fit_file)) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = "coxph fit file not found"
    ))
  }
  
  fit <- readRDS(fit_file)
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = paste("coxph fit is error object:", fit$message)
    ))
  }
  
  zph <- tryCatch(
    cox.zph(fit),
    error = function(e) e
  )
  
  if (inherits(zph, "error")) {
    return(list(
      model_id = model_id,
      ph_ok    = NA,
      zph_tbl  = NULL,
      error    = as.character(zph$message)
    ))
  }
  
  plot_file <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(model_id, "_schoenfeld.png"))
  png(plot_file, width = 1600, height = 1200, res = 150)
  par(mfrow = c(ceiling(nrow(zph$table) / 2), 2))
  plot(zph)
  dev.off()
  
  zph_tbl <- as.data.frame(zph$table)
  zph_tbl$term <- rownames(zph_tbl)
  
  zph_tbl <- zph_tbl %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::filter(term != "GLOBAL") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model_id = model_id, .before = 1)
  
  ph_ok <- !any(zph_tbl$p < alpha, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  list(
    model_id = model_id,
    ph_ok    = ph_ok,
    zph_tbl  = zph_tbl,
    error    = NA_character_
  )
}

      error = function(e) e
    )
    saveRDS(fit, out_file)
  }
  
  if (inherits(fit, "error")) {
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      formula    = row$formula_coxph_chr,
      logLik     = NA_real_,
      AIC        = NA_real_,
      deltaAIC   = NA_real_,
      weight     = NA_real_,
      nparams    = NA_integer_,
      message    = as.character(fit$message)
    )
  } else {
    LL     <- logLik(fit)
    ll_num <- as.numeric(LL)
    df     <- attr(LL, "df")
    aic    <- -2 * ll_num + 2 * df
    
    tibble::tibble(
      model_id   = model_id,
      formula    = row$formula_coxph_chr,
      logLik     = ll_num,
      AIC        = aic,
      deltaAIC   = NA_real_,
      weight     = NA_real_,
      nparams    = df,
      message    = NA_character_
    )
  }
}

plan(multisession, workers = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))

    future_map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df_batch)), function(i) {
      fit_one_coxph(df_batch[i, ], dat = dat, dir_models = dir_models)
    })
  })

# 11. MODEL AVERAGING ####
##  11.1: Build list ranked by AIC (MuMIn::model.sel), incl. null model (no covariates)
##  11.2: Subset top models by ΔAIC threshold
##  11.3: Extract coefficients & HRs from top model
##  11.4: Model-averaged coefficients

deltaAIC_threshold <- 2

coxph_fit_summary <- read.csv(out_file_summary)

valid_models <- coxph_fit_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(AIC) & is.finite(AIC))

model_ids <- valid_models$model_id

all_fits <- lapply(model_ids, function(mid) {
  readRDS(file.path(dir_models, paste0(mid, "_coxph.rds")))
})
names(all_fits) <- model_ids

## 11.1: null model: Surv(...) ~ 1 (+ strata() if specified)
null_formula_str <- paste0(
  response_str, " ~ 1",
  if (length(strat_vars) > 0) {
    paste0(" + strata(", paste(strat_vars, collapse = ", "), ")")
  } else {
    ""
  }
)
null_formula <- as.formula(null_formula_str)
null_fit     <- coxph(null_formula, data = dat, ties = "efron")

null_model_id <- "M0_null"

all_fits_with_null <- c(
  setNames(list(null_fit), null_model_id),
  all_fits
)

models_all <- do.call(
  MuMIn::model.sel,
  c(all_fits_with_null, list(rank = "AIC"))
)

models_all_df <- as.data.frame(models_all)
models_all_df$model_id <- rownames(models_all_df)
models_all_df <- models_all_df %>%
  dplyr::select(model_id, dplyr::everything()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(AIC)

all_list_file <- file.path(outdir_root, "coxph_model_selection_all_MuMIn.csv")

write.csv(
  models_all_df,
  all_list_file,
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Full coxph model selection table (MuMIn, including null) saved to:\n",
    all_list_file, "\n")


## 11.2: Top candidate models (excluding null)
top_models <- subset(
  models_all,
  rownames(models_all) != null_model_id & delta <= deltaAIC_threshold
)

top_models_df <- as.data.frame(top_models)
top_models_df$model_id <- rownames(top_models_df)
top_models_df <- top_models_df %>%
  dplyr::select(model_id, dplyr::everything()) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(AIC)

top_list_file <- file.path(
  outdir_root,
  paste0("coxph_model_selection_deltaAIC_", deltaAIC_threshold, "_MuMIn.csv")
)

write.csv(
  top_models_df,
  top_list_file,
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Top coxph models (ΔAIC <=", deltaAIC_threshold,
    ", excluding null) from MuMIn saved to:\n",
    top_list_file, "\n")


## 11.3: Top model coefficients
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; top-model coefficient table not created.")
} else {
  best_model_name <- rownames(top_models)[1]
  best_fit        <- all_fits_with_null[[best_model_name]]
  
  beta <- coef(best_fit)
  vc   <- as.matrix(vcov(best_fit))
  se   <- sqrt(diag(vc))
  
  z_val <- beta / se
  p_val <- 2 * stats::pnorm(abs(z_val), lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  top_model_coefs <- tibble::tibble(
    term         = names(beta),
    estimate     = as.numeric(beta),
    se           = as.numeric(se),
    z_value      = as.numeric(z_val),
    p_value      = as.numeric(p_val),
    HR           = as.numeric(HR),
    HR_lower_95  = as.numeric(HR_lower_95),
    HR_upper_95  = as.numeric(HR_upper_95),
    model_id     = best_model_name
  )
  
  out_file_top <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_top_model_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    top_model_coefs,
    out_file_top,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("Top coxph model coefficients (with HR and 95% CI) saved to:\n",
      out_file_top, "\n")
}


## 11.4: Model-averaged coefficients
if (nrow(top_models_df) == 0) {
  warning("No non-null models with delta <= ", deltaAIC_threshold,
          "; model averaging skipped.")
} else {
  avg_fit <- MuMIn::model.avg(top_models)
  avg_sum <- summary(avg_fit)
  
  avg_coefs <- as.data.frame(avg_sum$coefmat.full)
  avg_coefs$term <- rownames(avg_coefs)
  
  est_col <- "Estimate"
  se_col  <- if ("Std. Error" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "Std. Error"
  } else if ("SE" %in% names(avg_coefs)) {
    "SE"
  } else {
    stop("Could not identify standard error column in avg_coefs.")
  }
  
  beta <- avg_coefs[[est_col]]
  se   <- avg_coefs[[se_col]]
  
  HR          <- exp(beta)
  HR_lower_95 <- exp(beta - 1.96 * se)
  HR_upper_95 <- exp(beta + 1.96 * se)
  
  avg_coefs$HR          <- HR
  avg_coefs$HR_lower_95 <- HR_lower_95
  avg_coefs$HR_upper_95 <- HR_upper_95
  
  avg_coefs <- avg_coefs %>%
    dplyr::select(
      term,
      dplyr::everything()
    )
  
  out_file_avg <- file.path(
    outdir_root,
    paste0("coxph_model_averaged_coeffs_MuMIn_deltaAIC_",
           deltaAIC_threshold, ".csv")
  )
  
  write.csv(
    avg_coefs,
    out_file_avg,
    row.names = FALSE
  )
  
  cat("MuMIn model-averaged coxph coefficients (with HR and 95% CI) saved to:\n",
      out_file_avg, "\n")
}

# Write a function that allows CIs to be plotted as steps
make_step_ribbon <- function(df) {
  # df must have columns: time, surv, lower, upper (plus grouping cols)
  df <- df[order(df$time), ]

  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(df)

  # start and end times for each step
  time_start <- df$time
  time_end   <- c(df$time[-1], df$time[nrow(df)])  # last step ends at last time

  # replicate each row twice
  out <- df[rep(seq_len(nrow(df)), each = 2), ]

  # assign stepped times: (t_i, t_{i+1}) for each original row
  out$time <- c(rbind(time_start, time_end))

  out
}

# Update CIs to be plotted as steps
plot_dat_step <- plot_dat_boot %>%
  dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ make_step_ribbon(.x)) %>%

V <- vcov(m1)

HR  <- exp(beta_hat)
CI  <- exp(beta_hat + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * se_hat)
```

```{r prepare_PIT_data_for_survival_analysis, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# Prepare PIT tag detection data for survival analysis

# 1. Combine PIT release data and detection data into a single data set ####
foo1 <- PIT.smolts %>%
  dplyr::select(Tag_ID, Release_DateTime, Age_Class, FL_mm, Mass_g, Tag_Burden) 

foo2 <- PIT.dets %>%
  dplyr::select(Tag_ID, DateTime, Trap_No)

str(foo1)
str(foo2)

PIT_fence_arrivals <- foo1 %>%
  dplyr::left_join(foo2, by = "Tag_ID")

remove(foo1, foo2)

# To avoid issues w/ some packages used later, format PIT_fence_arrivals as a data.frame
PIT_fence_arrivals <- as.data.frame(PIT_fence_arrivals)

# 2. Create a column that codes whether a smolt arrived at the fence (i.e., whether the event of interest occurred) ####
PIT_fence_arrivals <- PIT_fence_arrivals %>%
  dplyr::mutate(status = dplyr::if_else(!is.na(DateTime), 1, 0))

table(PIT_fence_arrivals$status)

# Summarize fence arrival by age class
PIT_fence_arrivals %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Age_Class, status) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(n = length(Tag_ID))

# 3. Censor smolts that were never detected ####

# For the PIT-tagged smolts that were not detected at the fence, we can't draw any conclusions about their migration success from release to the fence.
# So, we must censor these smolts prior to survival analysis; it is also possible that we remove them entirely, but we'll start with censoring.

# Individuals with unknown status should be censored at the time of their last observation or detection.
# For PIT-tagged smolts that were never detected at the fence, the date of last observation is the date and time of their release.
# So, for any smolts that were not detected at the fence, the DateTime column (i.e., Date & Time of event) should match the Release_DateTime column.
# In case there are issues caused by censoring the smolts at the same time as they were released, we will censor non-detected smolts 30 seconds after release.
PIT_fence_arrivals <- PIT_fence_arrivals %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DateTime = dplyr::if_else(status == 1, DateTime, Release_DateTime + lubridate::seconds(30)))

# Calculate time difference between release and fence crossing or censoring for each fish
# Time difference is calculated as days, hours, and seconds
PIT_fence_arrivals <- PIT_fence_arrivals %>%
  dplyr::mutate(days_to_event = as.numeric(difftime(DateTime, Release_DateTime, units = "days"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(hours_to_event = as.numeric(difftime(DateTime, Release_DateTime, units = "hours"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(seconds_to_event = as.numeric(difftime(DateTime, Release_DateTime, units = "secs")))

# 4. Release groups ####

# Smolts were released in eight groups over the course of ~12 days 
# Create a grouping variable for release groups
PIT_fence_arrivals <- PIT_fence_arrivals %>%
  dplyr::mutate(release_group = case_when(Release_DateTime == "2014-04-29 00:40:00" ~ "1",
                                          Release_DateTime == "2014-04-30 00:25:00" ~ "2",
                                          Release_DateTime == "2014-04-30 23:55:00" ~ "3",
                                          Release_DateTime == "2014-05-02 00:05:00" ~ "4",
                                          Release_DateTime == "2014-05-03 00:05:00" ~ "5",
                                          Release_DateTime == "2014-05-08 00:15:00" ~ "6",
                                          Release_DateTime == "2014-05-10 00:10:00" ~ "7",
                                          Release_DateTime == "2014-05-11 00:10:00" ~ "8"))

# Format the release group variable as a factor
PIT_fence_arrivals$release_group <- as.factor(PIT_fence_arrivals$release_group)

# 5. Tag type ####

# Add a column for tag type to differentiate between VPS (acoustic tag) and PIT tag
PIT_fence_arrivals <- PIT_fence_arrivals %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tag_type = "PIT")


```

```{r combine_PIT_and_acoustic_data, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# 1. Set up the data ####

# For each acoustic-tagged smolt, update the event time in fence_arrivals w/ the event time in cr_cox_data_main

# First, discard any periods of occupation in Zone 4
# These are filtered out prior to compiling unique zone- and rate-specific data sets for the competing-risk approach
# If these rows are not filtered, the max value for tstop_datetime will not correspond to event time for smolts that passed the fence
cr_cox_data_subset <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::filter(zone != "Z4")

# This was supposed to slice the release date time, but for some smolts it didn't.
cr_start <- cr_cox_data_subset %>%
  dplyr::select(fish_id, tstart_datetime) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(fish_id) %>%
  dplyr::slice_min(tstart_datetime)

cr_end <- cr_cox_data_subset %>%
  dplyr::select(fish_id, tstop_datetime, event) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(fish_id) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(tstop_datetime)

cr_events <- cr_start %>%
  dplyr::left_join(cr_end, by = "fish_id")

# Update the event column to reflect passage (1) and censoring (0)
cr_events <- cr_events %>%
  dplyr::mutate(event = if_else(event == "4", 1, 0))

# Format the dataset for combination w/ PIT data
foo <- cr_cox_data_main %>%
  dplyr::select(fish_id, FL_mm, mass_g, tag_burden, release_group, K) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(age_class = "2",
                tag_type = "Acoustic") %>%
  tidyr::unite(tag_age, tag_type, age_class, sep = "-", remove = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

acoustic <- cr_events %>%
  dplyr::left_join(foo, by = "fish_id")

# Add a row for smolt 173 that was never detected
s173 <- VPS.smolts %>%
  dplyr::filter(Fish_ID == "173") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tstop_datetime = NA,
                event = 0,
                K = (Mass_g / (FL_mm^3) ) * 100000,
                tag_age = "Acoustic-2",
                tag_type = "Acoustic") %>%
  dplyr::select(Fish_ID, Release_DateTime, tstop_datetime, event, FL_mm, Mass_g, Tag_Burden, release_group, K, tag_age, Age_Class, tag_type) %>%
  dplyr::rename(fish_id = Fish_ID,
                tstart_datetime = Release_DateTime,
                mass_g = Mass_g,
                tag_burden = Tag_Burden,
                age_class = Age_Class)

acoustic <- acoustic %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(s173)

remove(VPS.smolts, s173)

# Format PIT data for combination with acoustic
foo1 <- PIT_fence_arrivals %>% 
  dplyr::select(Tag_ID, Release_DateTime, DateTime, status, release_group) %>%
  dplyr::rename(fish_id = Tag_ID,
                tstart_datetime = Release_DateTime,
                tstop_datetime = DateTime,
                event = status)
  
foo2 <- PIT.smolts %>%
  dplyr::select(Tag_ID, FL_mm, Mass_g, Age_Class, Tag_Burden) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(K = (Mass_g / (FL_mm^3) ) * 100000,
                tag_type = "PIT") %>%
  dplyr::rename(fish_id = Tag_ID,
                mass_g = Mass_g,
                age_class = Age_Class,
                tag_burden = Tag_Burden) %>%
  tidyr::unite(tag_age, tag_type, age_class, sep = "-", remove = FALSE)

pit <- foo1 %>%
  dplyr::left_join(foo2, by = "fish_id")
  
pit <- pit %>%
  dplyr::relocate(fish_id, tstart_datetime, tstop_datetime, event, FL_mm, mass_g, tag_burden, release_group, K, tag_age, age_class, tag_type)


# Because PIT smolts could only be detected if they passed the fence, we need to censor all PIT smolts that did not pass the fence
# There's two ways to approach this: 
# 1. We could censor PIT smolts that did not pass the fence at the time of their last observation, which would correspond to their release time (though, we will use release timestamp + 5 minutes)
# If this approach is used, VPS smolts can stay censored at the time of final observation, which is the current time in acoustic data set

# 2. We could assume that any smolt that did not pass the fence is upstream of the fence, and censor those smolts at the end of the study.
# This approach is not typical for TTE analysis, but it would give us a better understanding of the proportion of released smolts that passed the fence over time. This approach would require updating the tstop_datetime for all smolts  (PIT and acoustic) with an event of 0 to the timestamp associated with the final record for fence operation (2014-05-20 23:55:00).

# We will use approach #2, but prepare the data for both scenarios

# Prepare the acoustic and PIT data for both scenarios; the correct observed censor and event times for acoustic smolts are in cr_events

# PIT smolts
pit <- pit %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
                tstop_observed_datetime = case_when(event == 1 ~ tstop_datetime,
                                                    event == 0 ~ tstart_datetime + 300),
                tstop_expire_datetime = case_when(event == 1 ~ tstop_datetime,
                                                  event == 0 ~ as.POSIXct("2014-05-20 23:55:00", tz = "Canada/Pacific"))) %>%
  
  # Only retain columns needed for analysis
  dplyr::mutate(
    tstop_observed_censor = as.numeric(difftime(tstop_observed_datetime, tstart_datetime, units = "days")),
    tstop_expire_censor = as.numeric(difftime(tstop_expire_datetime, tstart_datetime, units = "days"))) %>%
  
    dplyr::select(fish_id, tstart_datetime, tstop_observed_datetime, tstop_observed_censor, 
                tstop_expire_datetime, tstop_expire_censor, event, release_group, FL_mm, mass_g, K, 
                age_class, tag_type, tag_burden, tag_age)
  
  
# Acoustic smolts
acoustic <- acoustic %>%
  # Fill NA values for smolt 173 (never detected)
  #dplyr::mutate(tstart_datetime = case_when(fish_id == "173" ~ Release_DateTime, 
  #                                          fish_id != "173" ~ tstart_datetime)) %>%
  
  # censor smolt 173 at 5-minutes post release (this will be the observed censoring time for the smolt that was never detected)
  dplyr::mutate(tstop_datetime = case_when(fish_id == "173" ~ tstart_datetime + 300,
                                           fish_id != "173" ~ tstop_datetime)) %>%
  
  # create tstop columns for observed censor time and terminal censor time (end of study period)
  dplyr::mutate(tstop_observed_datetime = tstop_datetime,
                tstop_expire_datetime = case_when(event == 1 ~ tstop_datetime, 
                                                  event == 0 ~ as.POSIXct("2014-05-20 23:55:00", tz = "Canada/Pacific"))) %>%
  
  # Only retain columns needed for analysis
  dplyr::mutate(
    tstop_observed_censor = as.numeric(difftime(tstop_observed_datetime, tstart_datetime, units = "days")),
    tstop_expire_censor = as.numeric(difftime(tstop_expire_datetime, tstart_datetime, units = "days"))) %>%
  
    dplyr::select(fish_id, tstart_datetime, tstop_observed_datetime, tstop_observed_censor, 
                tstop_expire_datetime, tstop_expire_censor, event, release_group, FL_mm, mass_g, K, 
                age_class, tag_type, tag_burden, tag_age)


# Combine PIT and acoustic data
PIT_acoustic_events <- rbind(acoustic, pit)

# Remove objects not needed
keep <- c("PIT_acoustic_events", "fence.openings")
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), keep))

# Now, we can:
# - 1. calculate correlation among covariates
# - 2. fit models to compare passage rates
# - 3. we will want to first establish the covariates of interest, and then fit models for both censoring scenarios 

# 2. Test for collinearity ####

covs <- PIT_acoustic_events %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(FL_mm, K, tag_burden, age_class, tag_type, tag_age, release_group) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

# Transform categorical variables into numeric dummy variables
covs <- covs %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_class = dplyr::case_when(
    age_class == "1" ~ 0,
    age_class == "2" ~ 1),
    
    tag_type = case_when(
      tag_type == "PIT" ~ 0,
      tag_type == "VPS" ~ 1),
    
    tag_age = case_when(
      tag_age == "age-1, PIT" ~ 0,
      tag_age == "age-2, PIT" ~ 1,
      tag_age == "age-2, VPS" ~ 2),
    
    release_group = case_when(
      release_group == "1" ~ 0,
      release_group == "2" ~ 1,
      release_group == "3" ~ 2,
      release_group == "4" ~ 3,
      release_group == "5" ~ 4,
      release_group == "6" ~ 5,
      release_group == "7" ~ 6,
      release_group == "8" ~ 7))


covs <- covs %>%
  dplyr::select(c(K, release_group, FL_mm, tag_burden, age_class))
    

# Calculate correlation between the features
K_matrix <- covs %>%
  dplyr::mutate_if(is.factor, as.numeric) %>% # Converting factors to numeric
  as.matrix()

# Compute the correlation matrix from 'cor' function
cor_K_matrix <- stats::cor(K_matrix, method = "pearson")

# Rendering
cor_K_matrix %>% 
  round(2) %>% 
  knitr::kable() %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 9)

# Plot the correlation matrix
library(corrplot)
corrplot(cor_K_matrix, type = "upper", order = "hclust", method = "number",
         tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45, mar = c(0,0,0,0), tl.cex = 0.75)

PIT_acoustic_events %>%
  dplyr::group_by(tag_type, age_class) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(min = min(tag_burden),
                   max = max(tag_burden))


# Covariates that are safe to retain:
# - K
# - Release group
# - FL
# - tag burden

# Note: We could investigate other covariates that are not included b/c of collinearity
# For instance, age class is highly collinear w/ FL
# But, we need to consider what's more informative - the effect of smolt size, or age?
# The same could be said for tag type or the age-tag composite covariate
# Using FL allows us to investigate biological effects, and we can generate predictions for the average lengths observed for each age class.

# Based on correlation matrix, we won't retain discharge or tag burden

# Compute VIFs
library(car)
lm_fit <- lm(rep(1, nrow(covs)) ~ release_group + FL_mm + K + tag_burden, 
             data = covs)
as.data.frame(vif(lm_fit))

# From here, we can fit a cox PH model that incorporates >1 covariate, but we can also fit separate log-rank tests for each covariate of interest. Then, decide what covariate effect is most compelling.

# 3. Cox PH model structure description ####

# We will take two approaches to model construction that will let us ask different questions while avoiding issues of collinearity:

# 1. Mechanistic models - Is passage time influenced by physiological traits and internal tag load?

# 2. Tagging method models - Does the tagging procedure and age differences influence passage?
 
# To evaluate static predictors of fence passage time while avoiding collinearity, we used two complementary model structures. The first model included fish length, condition, and tag burden, with release group fitted as a frailty term, to test whether continuous physiological traits or internal tag load influenced passage; in this model, we also evaluated tag burden × length and tag burden × condition interactions because the effects of tag load are expected to be stronger for smaller or poorer-condition fish.

# For the second model, we used a combined three-level covariate (age-1 PIT, age-2 PIT, and age-2 acoustic) rather than separate age and tag-type terms, because age-1 fish were never acoustic-tagged, leaving an empty age-1 acoustic category and preventing estimation of all contrasts in an age × tag-type interaction. The combined covariate therefore provides identifiable group comparisons and allows direct evaluation of whether age-2 acoustic-tagged fish (who undergo more invasive surgery) exhibited delayed passage relative to PIT-tagged fish of either age class. A release-group frailty term was again included to account for group-level heterogeneity.

# 4. Add fence operation information ####

# The fence status (open vs. closed) needs to be incorporated before any other step so that we can identify risk states associated with periods that the fence was open "at risk" vs closed "not at risk" (for the multi-state model)

# First, create a new data set where each row is a new fence status
library(data.table)

# Convert to data.table for easier grouping by run-length encoding
dt <- as.data.table(fence.openings)

# Create a group identifier for runs of the same fence_status
dt[, group := rleid(fence_status)]

# Collapse intervals where fence_status is "open" (we don't care about transitions between 1 vs 2 traps open)
collapsed <- dt[, .(
  Start = min(Start),
  End = max(End),
  fence_status = first(fence_status)
), by = group][, .(Start, End, fence_status)]  # Drop the 'group' column

collapsed <- collapsed %>%
  dplyr::rename(DateTime_Start = Start,
                DateTime_End = End)

collapsed <- as_tibble(collapsed)

# Check that this worked as intended by referencing the fence.openings data set
fence_events_list <- list()

for (i in 1:nrow(PIT_acoustic_events)) {
  fish <- PIT_acoustic_events[i, ]
  start <- fish$tstart_datetime
  stop <- fish$tstop_expire_datetime # We're using the administrative right-censoring as opposed to observed censoring
  
  fence_sub <- collapsed %>%
    dplyr::filter(DateTime_End > start, DateTime_Start < stop) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(fish_id = fish$fish_id,
                  tchange = as.numeric(difftime(DateTime_Start, start, units = "days"))) %>%
    dplyr::select(fish_id, tchange, fence_status)
  
  fence_events_list[[i]] <- fence_sub
}

fence_events_all <- bind_rows(fence_events_list) %>%
  arrange(fish_id, tchange)

# For some reason, tchange = 0 is negative for the first fence status in every interval,
# even though the fence status at the start of each interval was correctly assigned.

# For example, the first observation for smolt 100 (100_Z2_1, since release was in zone 2) has a tchange value of -0.41666667 and a fence status of 'closed'. 
# This smolt was release on Apr. 30 at 00:25:00, and the fence was closed 25 minutes (~0.417 hours) earlier at 00:00:00. 
# So, the fence_status is correct, but the value of -0.417 in tchange is indicating that the fence was closed 0.417 hours (25 minutes) before the smolt was released.
# Change all negative values for tchange to 0

fence_events_all <- fence_events_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tchange = if_else(tchange < 0, 0, tchange))


# Base `tmerge`
tdata1 <- tmerge(data1 = PIT_acoustic_events,
                 data2 = PIT_acoustic_events,
                 id = fish_id,
                 event = event(tstop_expire_censor, event))

# Add fence_status as time-varying covariate
tdata2 <- tmerge(data1 = tdata1,
                 data2 = fence_events_all,
                 id = fish_id,
                 fence_status = tdc(tchange, fence_status))

# Check that no smolts pass the fence when it's closed
foo <- tdata2 %>%
  dplyr::filter(event == 1 & fence_status == "closed")

# Now, I can fit models stratified on fence status

pit_acoustic_events_long <- tdata2

```

```{r model_fitting_and_data_summaries, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}

# 1. Fit models and address violation of assumptions ####

dat <- pit_acoustic_events_long %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    z.FL = as.numeric(scale(FL_mm)),
    z.K = as.numeric(scale(K)),
    z.burden = as.numeric(scale(tag_burden))
  )

# Tag burden Cox PH model
burden_mod <- coxph(Surv(tstart,tstop, event) ~ z.burden + frailty(release_group, distribution = "gaussian") + strata(fence_status), data = dat)

# Age-Tag type Cox PH model
age_tag_mod <- coxph(Surv(tstart,tstop, event) ~ tag_age + frailty(release_group, distribution = "gaussian") + strata(fence_status), data = dat)

# FL & K Cox PH model
fl_k_mod <- coxph(Surv(tstart,tstop, event) ~ z.FL + z.K + frailty(release_group, distribution = "gaussian") + strata(fence_status), data = dat)


# Check model assumptions.
cox.zph(burden_mod)
plot(cox.zph(burden_mod))
cox.zph(age_tag_mod)
plot(cox.zph(age_tag_mod, transform = "identity"))
cox.zph(fl_k_mod)
plot(cox.zph(fl_k_mod, transform = "identity"))

# Address assumption violations and re-fit models
# Violation for FL needs to be addressed w/ a linear transformation, but a split at ~8 days post-release could also work
# Violation for age-tag could be addressed w/a time split at ~ 2 days post-release, but it could also be ignored (minor violation)
# The tag burden model does not violate the PH assumption

dat_split_fl <- survSplit(Surv(tstop, event) ~ .,dat, cut = 8, episode = "time_group_fl")

fl_k_mod <- coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ z.FL:strata(time_group_fl) + z.K + frailty(release_group, distribution = "gaussian") + strata(fence_status), data = dat_split_fl)

dat_split_tag_age <- survSplit(Surv(tstop, event) ~ .,dat, cut = 10, episode = "time_group_tag_age")

summary(burden_mod)
summary(age_tag_mod)
summary(fl_k_mod)

# 2. Plot scenario-based cumulative event curves for age-tag groups ####

# Scenario-based curves plot predicted effects over a user-defined fence schedule 
# In this case, we use the observed fence operation schedule from the start of the study to the last day of smolt tracking

# Define ID column
id_var <- "fish_id" 

# 1) Fit matching no-frailty model ONLY to get stratum baseline hazards
age_tag_base <- coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ tag_age + strata(fence_status), data = dat, ties = "efron", x = TRUE)

# 2) Extract baseline cumulative hazard by stratum
bh <- basehaz(age_tag_base, centered = FALSE)
# bh columns typically: time, hazard, strata

# Parse strata label into fence_status values
# Often looks like "fence_status=open"
bh <- bh %>%
  dplyr::mutate(fence_status = sub("^fence_status=", "", strata)) %>%
  dplyr::select(time, hazard, fence_status)

# Build step-function that evaluates H0_status(t) for each stratum
make_H0_fun <- function(bh_status) {
  # step function for cumulative hazard H0(t)
  # approx(..., method="constant") gives right-continuous steps like basehaz
  function(t) {
    approx(x = bh_status$time,
           y = bh_status$hazard,
           xout = t,
           method = "constant",
           f = 0, # right-continuous
           rule = 2 # extend ends
           )$y
  }
}

H0_funs <- bh %>%
  group_by(fence_status) %>%
  group_map(~ make_H0_fun(.x), .keep = TRUE)

names(H0_funs) <- bh %>% distinct(fence_status) %>% pull()

# 3) Derive a fence schedule from a smolt that was monitored for the full study period
# This will be a smolt from the first release group that did not pass the fence 

# Pick the individual with the longest continuous observation window (by span)
# Then use their rows as the scenario schedule.
dat_id <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.id = .data[[id_var]]) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(tmin = min(tstart, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmax = max(tstop,  na.rm = TRUE),
                   span = tmax - tmin,
                   n = n(),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(span), desc(n))

chosen_id <- dat_id$.id[1]

schedule <- dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(.id = .data[[id_var]]) %>%
  dplyr::filter(.id == chosen_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(tstart, tstop, fence_status) %>%
  dplyr::distinct() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(tstart, tstop)


# 4) Scenario cumulative baseline hazard function

# For a given time t, scenario H0(t) = sum over schedule intervals:
# H0_status(min(t, tstop_i)) - H0_status(tstart_i), for intervals that start < t

H0_scenario_at <- function(t, schedule, H0_funs) {
  # vectorized over t
  sapply(t, function(tt) {
    idx <- which(schedule$tstart < tt)
    if (length(idx) == 0) return(0)
    
    sum(vapply(idx, function(i) {
      stat <- as.character(schedule$fence_status[i])
      H0   <- H0_funs[[stat]]
      upper <- min(tt, schedule$tstop[i])
      if (upper <= schedule$tstart[i]) return(0)
      H0(upper) - H0(schedule$tstart[i])
    }, numeric(1)))
  })
}

# Choose a time grid to draw curves on:
# Use all baseline times (union across strata) + schedule boundaries
time_grid <- sort(unique(c(bh$time, schedule$tstart, schedule$tstop)))

H0_scen <- H0_scenario_at(time_grid, schedule, H0_funs)

# 5) Compute linear predictors from frailty model, setting frailty = 0 (linear predictor = coefficient estimate)

# strata() does not contribute to coef(); frailty not in coef()
beta <- coef(age_tag_mod)

# Build newdata scenarios for tag_age only (fence handled by schedule)
dat$tag_age <- as.factor(dat$tag_age)
newdat <- data.frame(tag_age = levels(dat$tag_age))

# LP using model matrix consistent with how coxph coded tag_age
X <- model.matrix(~ tag_age, data = newdat)
# Remove intercept column if present; coef() names should align automatically via matching
# Compute LP by matching coefficient names:
lp <- as.numeric(X[, names(beta), drop = FALSE] %*% beta)

newdat$lp <- lp

# 6) Build survival curves under the schedule
curves <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(newdat)), function(i) {
  eta <- newdat$lp[i]
  data.frame(
    time = time_grid,
    surv = exp(-H0_scen * exp(eta)),
    tag_age = newdat$tag_age[i]
  )
}))

# 7) Update group names

# Need to update group names to remove 'VPS' from the acoustic-tagged group
curves <- curves %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = case_when(tag_age == "PIT-1" ~ "age-1, PIT",
                                  tag_age == "PIT-2" ~ "age-2, PIT",
                                  tag_age == "Acoustic-2" ~ "age-2, acoustic")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("age-1, PIT", "age-2, PIT", "age-2, acoustic"))) 


# 8) Plot (include shading to depict fence operation schedule)
(plot_age_tag <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = schedule, aes(xmin = tstart, xmax = tstop, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = fence_status, alpha = fence_status)) +
  geom_step(data = curves, aes(x = time, y = 1-surv, colour = group), linewidth = 0.75) +
  labs(x = "Days After Release",
       y = "Proportion Passing",
       colour = "",
       fill = "Fence status",
       alpha = "Fence status") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.6)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("orange", "navy", "#009E73")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "grey90")) +

     guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = "black"))) +
 theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.text = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 14, family = "Helvetica", colour = "black"),
          axis.title.x = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 14, family = "Helvetica", margin = unit(c(10,0,0,0), "pt")),
          axis.title.y = ggtext::element_markdown(size = 14, family = "Helvetica", margin = unit(c(0,10,0,0), "pt"), 
                                                  lineheight = 1.2),
          axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.5, colour = "black", linetype = "solid"),
          axis.ticks.length = unit(0.2, "cm"),
          panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
          plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA, linewidth = 1),
          plot.margin = margin(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, "cm"),

# 4. Determine if any censored smolts were detected downstream ####

downstream_PIT <- read_csv("Data/downstream_PIT.csv")

downstream_VPS <- read_csv("Data/downstream_VPS.csv")

# Create a vector of smolt IDs for smolts that were detected downstream
foo1 <- downstream_PIT %>%
  dplyr::mutate(fish_id = as.character(ID)) %>%
  dplyr::select(fish_id)

foo2 <- downstream_VPS %>%
  dplyr::mutate(fish_id = as.character(Fish_ID)) %>%
  dplyr::select(fish_id)

foo3 <- rbind(foo1, foo2)

downstream_smolts <- foo3$fish_id

remove(foo1, foo2, foo3)

foo <- PIT_acoustic_events %>%
  dplyr::mutate(DS = if_else(fish_id %in% downstream_smolts & event == 0, 1, 0))

DS_smolts <- foo %>%
  dplyr::filter(DS == 1)

# 35 smolts that were censored during the study (assumed to have not passed the fence) were detected on receivers downstream of the fence.
```
